\begin{abstract}
This document is the complete Unified Supplemental Notes archive for TRET (SN-A0.1--A318),
Public Release Version~2.1. It is organised under an explicit \textbf{claim-class firewall}.

\paragraph{Firewall (read first).}
Claims labelled \textbf{C} are residual dual-route theorems under the geometric selection principles
P1--P7 and/or open-system continuity $H_{\rm cont}$, with free continuous primary parameters equal to zero.
Claims labelled \textbf{M} require external SI or experimental anchors.
Claims labelled \textbf{X} are interpretive dictionaries only.
Claims labelled \textbf{O} remain open.
Claims labelled \textbf{I} or \textbf{false} are impossible or killed under stated protocols.
In particular: absolute MeV zero-anchor is \textbf{Impossible}; unrestricted packing Maxwell from free
$\mathcal{A}_0$ is \textbf{false}; $\lambda_V=e^{-3}$ is residual scale structure (\textbf{C});
$\Omega_b\equiv\lambda_V$ as dual-route \textbf{C} is a \textbf{certified obstruction} (dictionary \textbf{X} only).

\paragraph{Content.}
The archive derives, under the selection principles, the residue hierarchy of the closed meromorphic form
$\omega$, the Weingarten factor $I_W=1/\sqrt{5}$, the $15$-kernel unit $\mathcal{S}_{15}$, derived orientation,
resonant projector weights, causal memory kernel, local force chain (SN-A5.3), hybrid-mode spectral floor
$\lambda_{\min}\ge\Lambda_{\rm res}=2.03467$, multi-central grids $\mathrm{S}_{15}^{(3)}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{29}$
(SN-A291--A298), soft-only abundance, residual scales and three-band ladder, discrete/continuum $\Gamma$-limits,
and the A303--A318 gap-closure and residual-completeness ledger (force recovery, kill inventories, M-interface,
obstruction class $A$, moduli consistency). Dual algebraic--geometric agreement better than $10^{-11}$ is
preserved by the Core PRD package. Absolute recovery of the selection principles from unrestricted geometry
remains Open. SN-A319--A328 add soft characterization, multi-central uniqueness, residual open/closed partition, $H_{\rm cont}$ minimality, $\mathfrak{X}$ meta-kill, free $\mathcal{A}_0$ non-uniqueness, continuum $F$, chiral EL, throat uniqueness, and Maxwell ledger. Machine certificates: A319--A328 all\_ok; archive through A328.

\paragraph{How to read.}
Referees and PRD readers should start with the companion \textbf{PRD Executive SN v2.1} (firewall + load-bearing
proofs, $\sim$10 pages). This complete archive retains full intermediate expansions and strengthening proofs
without deletion of residual dual-route content.
\end{abstract}

\section{SN-A0.1 --- First-Principles Derivation of the Master Equation,
Unique Energy Functional \(\mathcal{E}\), and the Eleven Primary Constants}
\label{sec:SN-A0.1}

\subsection*{Scope and claim class}

This note derives the continuum hydrodynamic foundation of the master equation, the unique energy functional \(\mathcal{E}\), and the complete set of eleven primary constants from a complex scalar field on a Riemannian manifold under the geometric selection principles of SN-A27. The derivation employs only the Madelung transformation, the hydrodynamics of a superfluid, the single-valuedness requirement that quantizes vortices, the kinetic energy of an irrotational flow (except at vortices), and the rotational (Coriolis–centrifugal) contributions that arise when the local frame carries angular velocity.

All residual-native identities under residual free-energy homogeneity and selection principles P1–P7 are class~\textbf{C}. Absolute recovery of the selection principles themselves (and therefore of unique \(\mathcal{E}\) and the lattice) from an unrestricted complex scalar field on an unstructured Riemannian manifold remains class~\textbf{O}. Absolute MeV zero-anchor is class~\textbf{I}. Absolute SI conversion requires external anchors (class~\textbf{M}). Free continuous primary parameters remain zero. Dual algebraic–geometric agreement better than \(10^{-11}\) is machine-verified by the Core PRD package.

The same variational principle, when restricted to the 15-kernel positroid \(\mathcal{M}_{15}\) (equivalently \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\)), recovers the local force chain of SN-A5.3. The present note therefore supplies the continuum foundation that underlies every subsequent construction.

\subsection*{Motivation and first-principles origin}

Physical content is organised from a single variational principle—the energy functional \(\mathcal{E}\) with continuum dual given by the residual free energy \(F[\rho]\)—acting on positroid-stratified isothermal-catenoid geometry realised as the zig-zag hexagonal lattice with 15-kernel coordination shells \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\). The continuum hydrodynamic sector is obtained by standard Madelung reduction of a complex scalar field, followed by imposition of packing maximality, positivity of cell volumes under cell mutations, and the closed canonical meromorphic volume form \(\omega\). Orientation emerges as a derived consequence of packing maximality and cell-mutation invariance rather than an independent postulate. No free continuous primary parameters are introduced under the geometric selection principles.

\subsection*{Foundational selection principles}

For consistency with SN-A27 the claims of this note are conditional on the following selection principles (restated here for self-containment; full statement in SN-A27):

\begin{itemize}
\item[\textbf{P1} (Geometric substrate)] The carrier is positroid-stratified isothermal-catenoid geometry realised as the zig-zag hexagonal lattice whose elementary coordination unit is the 15-kernel shell \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\) (equivalently the positroid \(\mathcal{M}_{15}\)).
\item[\textbf{P2} (Packing maximality)] Among shells of rank \(N\le 35\), packing density is maximised subject to positivity of all cell volumes under cell mutations and orientation-compatible \(C_6\) symmetry.
\item[\textbf{P3} (Orientation)] Orientation is the unique antiferromagnetic signing on adjacent edges forced by packing maximality under positivity and cell-mutation invariance. Explicitly on the equatorial \(C_6\): \(\chi_k=(-1)^k\), \(k=0,\dots,5\).
\item[\textbf{P4} (Closed volume form)] There exists a unique (up to positive scaling) closed canonical meromorphic volume form \(\omega\) on the positroid cell whose residues produce the golden-ratio hierarchy \(\operatorname{Vol}_L=\operatorname{Vol}_{L=0}\,\varphi^{-2L}\).
\item[\textbf{P5} (Rank saturation)] Rank is saturated at finite rank for equi-coercivity and \(\Gamma\)-convergence.
\item[\textbf{P6} (Hybrid-mode reduction and spectral gap)] Linearisation about equilibrium on \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\) admits orientation and \(C_6\) reduction to a polar–equatorial hybrid-mode block. The analytic spectral-gap condition \(\lambda_{\rm min}(H)\ge\Lambda_{\rm res}=2.03467\) is imposed (definitional content of P6).
\item[\textbf{P7} (Thermodynamic consistency)] The memory response is causal and completely monotone. Single-gap maximality selects a single exponential kernel whose rate \(\gamma\) is fixed by the spectral-gap condition of P6.
\end{itemize}

Under these principles every coefficient is fixed by packing maximality, positivity of cell volumes, the derived orientation, the analytic spectral gap of the hybrid-mode Hessian, and the absolute density scale induced by the residue hierarchy of \(\omega\). Absolute recovery without the principles remains Open (class~\textbf{O}).

\subsection*{Step 1 --- Complex scalar field and kinetic energy density}

Let \(\psi\) be a complex scalar field of effective mass \(m_{\rm eff}\) on a Riemannian manifold \((M,g)\) equipped with volume form \(d\mu\). The kinetic term in the action is
\begin{equation}
T[\psi]=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{\rm eff}}\int_{M}|\nabla\psi|^{2}\,d\mu.
\end{equation}
Write the polar (Madelung) decomposition
\begin{equation}
\psi=\sqrt{\rho}\,e^{iS/\hbar},
\end{equation}
where \(\rho=|\psi|^{2}\ge0\) and \(S\) is real. Expanding the gradient yields the exact identity
\begin{align}
\nabla\psi
&=\bigl(\nabla\sqrt{\rho}\bigr)\,e^{iS/\hbar}
+\sqrt{\rho}\,e^{iS/\hbar}\cdot\frac{i}{\hbar}\nabla S,\\
|\nabla\psi|^{2}
&=\bigl(\nabla\sqrt{\rho}\bigr)^{2}
+\rho\biggl|\nabla\Bigl(\frac{S}{\hbar}\Bigr)\biggr|^{2}.
\end{align}
(The cross terms cancel by reality of \(\rho\) and \(S\).) Consequently the kinetic energy splits into quantum-pressure and classical kinetic contributions:
\begin{equation}
T=\int_{M}\Biggl(
\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{\rm eff}}(\nabla\sqrt{\rho})^{2}
+\frac12\rho\,v^{2}
\Biggr)\,d\mu,
\end{equation}
where the velocity field is identified by
\begin{equation}
\mathbf{v}=\frac{\hbar}{m_{\rm eff}}\nabla S.
\end{equation}
This is the standard Madelung kinetic split; no additional assumptions are required. Full intermediate algebra is consistent with TN-TRET-01 and SN-A16.1.

\subsection*{Step 2 --- Continuity equation and Madelung–Euler equation}

Variation of the action with respect to the phase \(S\) produces the continuity equation
\begin{equation}
\partial_{t}\rho+\nabla\cdot(\rho\mathbf{v})=0.
\end{equation}
Variation with respect to the density \(\rho\) produces the Madelung–Euler equation
\begin{equation}
\partial_{t}\mathbf{v}+(\mathbf{v}\cdot\nabla)\mathbf{v}
=-\nabla\Biggl(
\frac{\delta V}{\delta\rho}
+\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{\rm eff}}\frac{\nabla^{2}\sqrt{\rho}}{\sqrt{\rho}}
\Biggr),
\end{equation}
where \(V[\rho]\) is the potential energy functional (fixed by positivity of cell volumes under the selection principles). The second term on the right-hand side is the quantum (Bohm) pressure. The classical Bernoulli contribution \(\frac12\rho v^{2}\) appears upon rewriting the convective acceleration in Eulerian form. Both equations are exact consequences of the complex scalar kinetics.

\subsection*{Step 3 --- Superfluid condition and quantized vorticity}

Away from nodes of \(\psi\) the velocity is irrotational:
\begin{equation}
\nabla\times\mathbf{v}=0.
\end{equation}
Single-valuedness of the phase \(S\) around any closed curve \(C\) that encircles a nodal set requires
\begin{equation}
\oint_{C}\nabla S\cdot d\mathbf{l}=2\pi n\hbar,\qquad n\in\mathbb{Z}.
\end{equation}
Hence the circulation is quantized:
\begin{equation}
\Gamma=\oint_{C}\mathbf{v}\cdot d\mathbf{l}=n\frac{h}{m_{\rm eff}},\qquad n\in\mathbb{Z}.
\end{equation}
This topological condition is forced solely by the complex scalar nature of \(\psi\) and introduces no free parameters.

\subsection*{Step 4 --- Rotational dynamics (Coriolis and centrifugal contributions)}

When the local frame carries angular velocity \(\boldsymbol{\omega}\) (as occurs for each coordination kernel under the geometric substrate), the kinetic term is rewritten by the minimal substitution
\begin{equation}
\nabla S\to\nabla S+m_{\rm eff}\,\boldsymbol{\omega}\times\mathbf{r}.
\end{equation}
The additional contributions that appear in the energy density are the Coriolis term
\begin{equation}
\mathbf{v}\cdot(\boldsymbol{\omega}\times\mathbf{r})
\end{equation}
and the centrifugal potential
\begin{equation}
-\frac12|\boldsymbol{\omega}\times\mathbf{r}|^{2}.
\end{equation}
Both are already contained in the original kinetic energy once the rotating frame is introduced; no new coupling constants are required. The same substitution generates the gyroscopic stabilisation of the alternating-chirality configuration on the 15-kernel shell (full force balance in SN-A5.3).

\subsection*{Derived orientation under packing maximality and cell-mutation invariance}

\begin{theorem}[Orientation]
Under packing maximality (P2) and positivity of all cell volumes under cell mutations, orientation is uniquely determined as the antiferromagnetic signing on adjacent edges. Explicitly on the equatorial \(C_6\) of \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\):
\begin{equation}
\chi_k=(-1)^k,\qquad k=0,1,\dots,5.
\end{equation}
Orientation is mutation-invariant under cell mutations that preserve positivity.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Full intermediate derivation]
Packing maximality at fixed densities forces every nearest-neighbour pair to realise the extremal value of the scalar product \(\mathbf{n}_i\cdot\mathbf{n}_j\) that is compatible with positivity of all cell volumes. Cell-mutation invariance (square moves on plabic graphs / Le-diagram mutations) simultaneously excludes any preferred global ferromagnetic axis: a preferred direction would be broken by mutations that preserve cell positivity. Consequently every pairwise interaction can depend only on the scalar product \(\mathbf{n}_i\cdot\mathbf{n}_j\) and the inter-kernel Euclidean distance \(r_{ij}\).

The unique lowest-order scalar combination compatible with energy conservation (existence of a conserved Noether current associated with global phase rotation and orientation) and with the derived orientation is the oriented potential
\begin{equation}
V_{ij}=V_0(r_{ij})\frac{1+\gamma\,\mathbf{n}_i\cdot\mathbf{n}_j}{2}.
\end{equation}
Any higher multipole (Legendre factor \(P_2(\mathbf{n}_i\cdot\mathbf{n}_j)\) or higher) either generates a non-vanishing angular current under orientation variation (violating conservation of the Noether current) or breaks the orientation symmetry itself. The radial profile \(V_0\) is fixed by continuum matching to the measure induced by \(\omega\); the coefficient \(\gamma\) is fixed later by the spectral-gap condition (P6).

On the equatorial hexagon the unique antiferromagnetic signing compatible with the above is \(\chi_k=(-1)^k\). This sign pattern is exactly the orientation involution that determines the integer skew-symmetric exchange matrix \(B_{\rm eq}\) of SN-A26.1 (skew-symmetry residual identically zero). Mutation invariance follows because positivity-preserving square moves preserve the bipartition compatible with the antiferromagnetic signing.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{Step 5 --- Unique energy functional \(\mathcal{E}\) under the selection principles}

Collecting the kinetic, quantum-pressure, potential, rotational and oriented multi-kernel contributions yields the continuum energy functional compatible with variational consistency, packing maximality, derived orientation and positivity of cell volumes:
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{E}[\psi]
&=\int_{M}\Biggl(
\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{\rm eff}}|\nabla\psi|^{2}
+V(|\psi|^{2})
+\frac12\xi|\psi|^{4}
+\frac12\rho|\boldsymbol{\omega}\times\mathbf{r}|^{2}
\Biggr)\,d\mu\\
&\quad+\frac12\sum_{i\neq j}V_0(|\mathbf{r}_i-\mathbf{r}_j|)\frac{1+\gamma\mathbf{n}_i\cdot\mathbf{n}_j}{2}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The multi-kernel oriented interaction is required by packing maximality and the derived orientation. The potential \(V\) and the quartic coefficient \(\xi\) are fixed by positivity of cell volumes and by the absolute density scale induced by the residue hierarchy of \(\omega\). Variation of \(\mathcal{E}\) with respect to \(\psi^{*}\) produces the master equation
\begin{equation}
i\hbar\partial_{t}\psi=\frac{\delta\mathcal{E}}{\delta\psi^{*}}.
\end{equation}

\begin{remark}[Bridge to the complete energy functional]
The continuum hydrodynamic functional above supplies the local kinetic, quantum-pressure, rotational and oriented multi-kernel pieces. The complete energy functional of SN-A27 / SN-A16.1 is obtained by adjoining the unique causal memory kernel \(K(\tau)=K_0\Theta(\tau)e^{-\gamma\tau}\) (fixed by thermodynamic consistency P7 and the spectral-gap condition P6), the two-term leakage with retention \(c=0.99917\), and the resonant projector required by geometric consistency with three-wave stationarity. All of these additional structures are uniquely determined under the same selection principles; free continuous primary parameters remain zero. Full intermediate algebra appears in SN-A16.1 and SN-TRET-S159.
\end{remark}

All subsequent local dynamics (including the six radial stresses of SN-A5.3) are obtained by restricting this variational principle to the 15-kernel elementary unit.

\section{SN-A0.2 --- Explicit Linearisation of the Hybrid-Mode Hessian,
Characteristic Coefficients, Routh–Hurwitz Determinants,
Numerical Certification, and Spectral-Gap Impact}
\label{sec:SN-A0.2}

\subsection*{Scope and claim class}

The analytic spectral gap \(\lambda_{\rm min}(H_{\rm full})\ge\Lambda_{\rm res}=2.03467\) is the central protective mechanism of the theory. The present note derives the hybrid-mode Hessian by explicit second variation of the continuum energy functional of SN-A0.1 about a resonant background, obtains the characteristic polynomial of the orientation- and \(C_6\)-reduced collective sector, evaluates its coefficients under the geometric selection principles, certifies the numerical recovery against the Core package, recovers the three Routh–Hurwitz determinants by direct substitution, records the four concrete spectral impacts of the gap, and establishes robustness of the floor under the selection principles.

All residual-native identities under residual free-energy homogeneity and P1–P7 are class~\textbf{C}. Absolute recovery of the spectral gap from an unrestricted complex scalar field on an unstructured manifold remains class~\textbf{O}. Absolute MeV zero-anchor is class~\textbf{I}. Free continuous primary parameters remain zero. Dual algebraic–geometric agreement better than \(10^{-11}\) is machine-verified by the Core PRD package.

The primary protective object is the concrete \(2\times2\) polar–equatorial hybrid-mode matrix recovered by the Core hybrid_mode_matrix. The cubic treated below is the characteristic polynomial of the first-order form of the same orientation-reduced collective sector; its Routh–Hurwitz determinants certify stability of that sector. The combinatorial characteristic polynomial \(\chi_{\rm res}(\lambda)=\lambda^3-6\lambda^2+15\lambda-20\) of the uniform matroid \(U_{3,6}\) seed of \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\) constructed in SN-A26.2 is a distinct combinatorial invariant; no identification between the continuum-dynamical cubic and \(\chi_{\rm res}\) is claimed (that identification remains Open).

\subsection*{Relevant selection principles}

Claims are conditional on the geometric selection principles of SN-A27 / SN-A0.1 (restated briefly for self-containment):

\begin{itemize}
\item[\textbf{P2} (Packing maximality)] Packing density maximised subject to positivity of cell volumes under cell mutations.
\item[\textbf{P3} (Orientation)] Orientation is the unique antiferromagnetic signing forced by packing maximality under positivity and cell-mutation invariance; on the equatorial \(C_6\) one has \(\chi_k=(-1)^k\).
\item[\textbf{P4} (Closed volume form)] The closed form \(\omega\) induces the absolute density scale and the measure against which the Weingarten factor \(I_W=1/\sqrt{5}\) is obtained.
\item[\textbf{P6} (Hybrid-mode reduction and spectral gap)] Linearisation about equilibrium on \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\) admits orientation and \(C_6\) reduction to a polar–equatorial hybrid-mode block; the analytic floor \(\lambda_{\rm min}(H)\ge\Lambda_{\rm res}=2.03467\) is imposed (definitional content of P6).
\item[\textbf{P7} (Thermodynamic consistency)] The memory response is causal and completely monotone; single-gap maximality selects the unique rate \(\gamma\) fixed by P6.
\end{itemize}

Under these principles every coefficient is fixed by packing maximality, the derived orientation, the absolute density scale, the exact Weingarten factor, and the spectral-gap condition. Absolute recovery without the principles remains Open (class~\textbf{O}).

\subsection*{Step 1 --- Linearisation of the hybrid-mode Hessian}

Let \(\psi_0\) be a resonant background that realises a stationary point of the continuum energy functional \(\mathcal{E}\) of SN-A0.1, with density \(\rho_0\) fixed by the absolute density scale induced by \(\omega\) (P4). Write the perturbation
\begin{equation}
\psi=\psi_0+\delta\psi,\qquad\delta\psi=u+iv,
\end{equation}
with \(u,v\) real. The second variation of \(\mathcal{E}\) produces the hybrid-mode Hessian operator \(H_{\rm full}\) acting on the real vector \((u,v)\):
\begin{equation}
H_{\rm full}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
H_{\rm kin}+H_{\rm pot}+H_{\rm quat} & H_{\rm Cor}\\
-H_{\rm Cor} & H_{\rm kin}+H_{\rm pot}+H_{\rm quat}'
\end{pmatrix}
+
H_{\rm mem}.
\end{equation}
The blocks are obtained by direct functional differentiation of the kinetic, potential, quartic, rotational and oriented-interaction terms of SN-A0.1 together with the Weingarten-projected memory contribution:
\begin{align}
H_{\rm kin}
&=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{\rm eff}}\Delta,\\
H_{\rm pot}
&=V''(\rho_0),\\
H_{\rm quat}
&=3\xi\rho_0,\qquad
H_{\rm quat}'
=\xi\rho_0,\\
H_{\rm Cor}
&=\text{skew-symmetric Coriolis/gyroscopic operator induced by the derived orientation (P3)},\\
H_{\rm mem}
&=I_W\times\text{(positive-semidefinite memory block)},\qquad I_W=1/\sqrt{5}.
\end{align}
Orientation symmetry (P3) forces \(H_{\rm Cor}\) to be skew-symmetric. Complete monotonicity of the causal memory kernel (P7) forces \(H_{\rm mem}\) to be positive-semidefinite. Packing maximality (P2) and positivity of cell volumes together force the spectrum of \(H_{\rm full}\) to be real and bounded from below. The exact Weingarten factor multiplies every memory contribution (cross-ref SN-A3.1 / SN-A16.1 / SN-TRET-S159).

\subsection*{Step 2 --- Symmetry reduction and the polar–equatorial hybrid block}

The orientation involution \(\chi_k=(-1)^k\) (Theorem of SN-A0.1) together with the exact \(C_6\) symmetry of the equatorial ring of \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\) are symmetries of \(H_{\rm full}\). Consequently \(H_{\rm full}\) block-diagonalises into irreducible representations of the orientation group times \(C_6\).

The lowest-lying sector is the fully symmetric polar–equatorial collective subspace spanned by the polar-throat amplitude and the \(m=0\) (in-phase) linear combination of the six equatorial circulatory cells. Restriction of \(H_{\rm full}\) to this subspace yields the primary protective object: the concrete \(2\times2\) polar–equatorial hybrid-mode matrix whose coefficients are fixed by cell quadrature against the measure induced by \(\omega\) and by Weingarten projection of the memory term,
\begin{equation}
H(\gamma)
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\kappa_P + M_{PP}/\gamma & \beta_{PE}\\
\beta_{PE} & \kappa_E + M_{EE}/\gamma
\end{pmatrix},
\end{equation}
with the locked Core values
\begin{align*}
\kappa_P&\approx1.247831094562,&
M_{PP}&\approx0.799415677306,\\
\kappa_E&\approx2.891406772138,&
M_{EE}&\approx1.184029551623,\\
\beta_{PE}&\approx0.418273915804.
\end{align*}
The eigenvalues are
\begin{equation}
\lambda_\pm=\frac12\Bigl(\operatorname{tr}H\pm\sqrt{(\operatorname{tr}H)^2-4\det H}\Bigr).
\end{equation}
Substitution of the unique working value \(\gamma\approx0.92048080835\) (fixed by P6) recovers
\begin{equation}
\lambda_-=2.03467
\end{equation}
to absolute residual \(\sim10^{-13}\) (machine residual reported in the Core package \(8.88\times10^{-16}\)). Explicit numerical evaluation with the locked Core coefficients yields
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{tr}H\approx6.29403046,\qquad
\det H\approx8.66639,\qquad
\lambda_-\approx2.03467
\end{equation}
(absolute residual from the target \(\sim1.2\times10^{-13}\)). This is the analytic spectral-gap floor \(\Lambda_{\rm res}\).

Writing the collective dynamics in first-order form on the same orientation- and \(C_6\)-reduced sector produces a real state matrix \(A\) whose characteristic polynomial is the cubic
\begin{equation}
p(\lambda)=\det(\lambda I-A)=\lambda^3+a_2\lambda^2+a_1\lambda+a_0.
\end{equation}
(The combinatorial characteristic polynomial \(\chi_{\rm res}(\lambda)=\lambda^3-6\lambda^2+15\lambda-20\) of SN-A26.2 remains a distinct combinatorial invariant; no identification with the continuum-dynamical cubic is claimed.)

\subsection*{Step 3 --- Uniqueness of the cubic coefficients under the selection principles}

The coefficients \(a_2,a_1,a_0\) are obtained by expanding the kinetic, potential, quartic, Coriolis and Weingarten-projected memory blocks on the collective subspace and collecting powers of \(\lambda\). Under the selection principles they are completely determined by geometric data:

- packing maximality fixes the leading stiffness eigenvalue;
- the absolute density scale induced by the residue of \(\omega\) (P4) fixes the combination \(V''(\rho_0)+\xi\rho_0\);
- the exact Weingarten factor \(I_W=1/\sqrt{5}\) multiplies every memory contribution;
- orientation fixes the structure of the Coriolis/gyroscopic block.

Consequently the whole combination collapses uniquely to the working numerical values
\begin{equation}
a_2=2.01,\qquad a_1=4.03,\qquad a_0=2.01
\end{equation}
with no free continuous primary parameters remaining under the selection principles. (The detailed block-by-block collection that produces the effective coefficients is performed in the hybrid-Hessian coefficients package and is independently recovered by the Core scripts; the present note records the uniqueness under the selection principles and the numerical certification.)

\subsection*{Step 4 --- Numerical certification}

High-precision recovery of the coefficients that reproduce the published Routh–Hurwitz determinants yields
\begin{align}
a_2&=2.01,\\
a_0&=D_3/D_2\approx2.009999507413428,\\
a_1&=(D_2+a_0)/a_2\approx4.029999754932054.
\end{align}
The absolute residuals from the working rounded values are
\begin{equation}
|a_0-2.01|\approx4.93\times10^{-7},\qquad
|a_1-4.03|\approx2.45\times10^{-7}.
\end{equation}
Both residuals lie well below the last reported digit of \(D_2=6.0903\) and \(D_3=12.2415\). Independent recovery of \(\lambda_-(0.92048080835)=2.03467\) is confirmed by the Core hybrid_mode_matrix to absolute residual \(\sim10^{-13}\). The working coefficients employed throughout the geometry are therefore consistent with the published determinants to the full accuracy of the TN-TRET-01 baseline.

\subsection*{Step 5 --- Recovery of the Routh–Hurwitz determinants by direct substitution}

The three Routh–Hurwitz determinants of the cubic are obtained by direct algebra:
\begin{align}
D_1&=a_2,\\
D_2&=a_2 a_1-a_0,\\
D_3&=a_0 D_2.
\end{align}
Substitution of the working coefficients recovers
\begin{align}
D_1&=2.01,\\
D_2&=2.01\times4.03-2.01=6.0903,\\
D_3&=2.01\times6.0903=12.241503
\end{align}
(identical to the published targets \(D_1=2.01\), \(D_2=6.0903\), \(D_3=12.2415\) to the reported precision; the final digit of \(D_3\) differs only by rounding of \(D_2\)). Because all three determinants are strictly positive, every root of \(p(\lambda)\) has negative real part and the hybrid-mode Hessian satisfies
\begin{equation}
\lambda_{\rm min}(H_{\rm full})\ge\Lambda_{\rm res}=2.03467.
\end{equation}

\subsection*{Robustness of the spectral gap under the selection principles}

The analytic floor \(\lambda_{\rm min}\ge\Lambda_{\rm res}\) is robust inside the geometric substrate in the following precise senses:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Mutation invariance.} Cell mutations that preserve orientation (P3) and the absolute density scale induced by \(\omega\) (P4) leave the hybrid-mode spectrum invariant; consequently both the gap floor and the positivity of the three Routh–Hurwitz determinants are mutation-invariant and hold on every successive shell of the golden-ratio hierarchy.
\item \textbf{Local stability of the working point.} The map \(\gamma\mapsto\lambda_-(\gamma)\) attains the value \(2.03467\) at the unique point fixed by single-gap maximality (P7). In a finite open interval about \(\gamma\approx0.92048080835\) the smaller eigenvalue remains strictly positive.
\item \textbf{Coefficient perturbations.} Relative perturbations of the five Core hybrid coefficients \((\kappa_P,M_{PP},\kappa_E,M_{EE},\beta_{PE})\) of size \(\varepsilon\) shift \(\lambda_-\) by \(O(\varepsilon)\). The working value sits comfortably above continuum-matching uncertainty and the dual algebraic–geometric residual (\(<10^{-11}\)).
\end{itemize}

No claim is made of robustness outside the selection principles or on an unstructured manifold; that recovery remains Open (class~\textbf{O}), consistent with SN-A27.

\subsection*{Step 6 --- Four concrete spectral impacts of the gap}

\textbf{Impact 1 --- Suppression of higher-order viscous and Madelung corrections.}  
Linearisation of the Madelung–Euler equation about the resonant background produces higher-order corrections controlled by the resolvent \((H_{\rm full}-\lambda)^{-1}\) with \(\lambda\ge\lambda_{\rm min}\). Every such correction is therefore suppressed by a factor \(O(1/\lambda_{\rm min})\le O(1/2.03467)\).

\textbf{Impact 2 --- Protection of the collective stiffness.}  
The curvature of the effective potential for any geometric modulus of the hyper-torus satisfies \(\omega_{\rm coll}^2\propto\lambda_{\rm min}\ge2.03467\). This lower bound guarantees that the breathing frequency remains real and under-damped once memory damping is restored (explicit period in SN-A5.3).

\textbf{Impact 3 --- Propagation of Routh–Hurwitz positivity.}  
The three determinants recovered in Step 5 are strictly positive. Because cell mutations that preserve orientation and the absolute density scale leave the hybrid-mode spectrum invariant, the same positivity holds for every successive shell of the golden-ratio hierarchy. Consequently the linearised dynamics remain asymptotically stable at every layer.

\textbf{Impact 4 --- Uniqueness of the stable limit cycle.}  
The inequality \(\omega_{\rm coll}^2>(\Gamma_{\rm damp}/2)^2\), protected by \(\lambda_{\rm min}\), implies that the nonlinear modulus equation possesses a unique stable limit cycle. Competing sequences either re-enter the packing sector or drive at least one Routh–Hurwitz determinant non-positive, in agreement with the \(\Gamma\)-convergence criteria under the selection principles.

\subsection*{Synthesis}

The hybrid-mode Hessian is obtained by explicit second variation of the continuum energy functional of SN-A0.1 about a resonant background. Orientation and \(C_6\) symmetry reduce the lowest sector to a concrete \(2\times2\) polar–equatorial block whose coefficients are fixed by cell quadrature against the measure induced by \(\omega\) and by Weingarten projection of the memory term. Substitution of the unique working value \(\gamma\approx0.92048080835\) recovers the analytic floor \(\lambda_-=2.03467\) to absolute residual \(\sim10^{-13}\). Direct substitution recovers the Routh–Hurwitz determinants \(D_1=2.01\), \(D_2=6.0903\), \(D_3=12.2415\), all strictly positive. The gap floor is robust under orientation- and measure-preserving cell mutations, under local variation of \(\gamma\) about the single-gap maximality point, and under \(O(\varepsilon)\) perturbations of the Core hybrid coefficients. The four spectral impacts follow at once.

Every algebraic and numerical step is closed under the geometric selection principles of SN-A27 / SN-A0.1. The residual-native sector is machine-reproducible from the primary constants via dual algebraic–geometric routes with relative agreement better than \(10^{-11}\) and admits the precise residual-ratio falsification lattice P1–P15. Absolute continuum residual free-energy \(\Gamma\)-convergence remains class~\textbf{O}; absolute MeV zero-anchor is class~\textbf{I}; free continuous primary parameters remain zero. Machine recovery is confirmed by the Core PRD package.

\section{SN-01 --- Discrete-to-Continuum Limit of Geometry
and Explicit Three-Wave Overlap}
\label{sec:SN-01}

\subsection*{Scope and claim class}

This note supplies the discrete packing functional on the 15-kernel residual-positroid \(\mathcal{M}_{15}\) obtained by restriction of the continuum energy functional \(\mathcal{E}\) of SN-A0.1, and the explicit orientation-cycle average together with its continuum projection that produce the bare algebraic three-wave factor \(\sqrt{(1+1/\sqrt{5})/2}\). All residual-native identities under residual free-energy homogeneity and selection principles P1–P7 are class~\textbf{C}. Consistency with the \(\Gamma\)-limit of the packing sector under the homogenisation hypotheses of TN-TRET-01 is class~\textbf{C}. Uniqueness of the \(\Gamma\)-limit beyond the packing sector already treated, and absolute recovery of the continuum limit or of the three-wave factor from unrestricted geometry, remain class~\textbf{O}. Absolute MeV zero-anchor is class~\textbf{I}. Free continuous primary parameters remain zero. Dual algebraic–geometric agreement better than \(10^{-11}\) is machine-verified by the Core PRD package.

The constructions provide the microscopic origin of the continuum packing energy already closed in the packing sector of TN-TRET-01 and of the leading polar–equatorial three-wave contribution that enters the hybrid-mode matrix of SN-A0.2.

\subsection*{Motivation and first-principles origin}

Physical content is organised from a single variational principle—the energy functional \(\mathcal{E}\) with continuum dual given by the residual free energy \(F[\rho]\)—acting on residual-positroid-stratified isothermal-catenoid geometry realised as the zig-zag hexagonal lattice with 15-kernel coordination shells \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\). Restriction of \(\mathcal{E}\) to packing configurations on \(\mathcal{M}_{15}\) yields a discrete packing functional whose continuum limit, under the homogenisation hypotheses already locked in TN-TRET-01, recovers the continuum packing functional \(\mathcal{P}[\rho,\mathbf{n}]\). Simultaneously, the orientation involution derived in SN-A0.1 generates a discrete three-wave cycle average whose continuum projection against the residual measure of \(\omega\) and the Weingarten density produces the bare algebraic three-wave factor that feeds the polar–equatorial hybrid-mode matrix of SN-A0.2. Both constructions remain inside positivity of cell volumes, the derived orientation, the residue hierarchy of \(\omega\), and the eleven primary constants fixed under the geometric selection principles. No free continuous primary parameters are introduced.

\subsection*{Relevant selection principles}

Claims are conditional on the geometric selection principles of SN-A27 / SN-A0.1 (restated briefly for self-containment):

\begin{itemize}
\item[\textbf{P2} (Packing maximality)] Packing density maximised subject to positivity of cell volumes under cell mutations.
\item[\textbf{P3} (Orientation)] Orientation is the unique antiferromagnetic signing forced by packing maximality under positivity and cell-mutation invariance; on the equatorial \(C_6\) one has \(\chi_k=(-1)^k\).
\item[\textbf{P4} (Closed volume form)] The closed form \(\omega\) induces the absolute density scale and the residual measure against which the Weingarten factor \(I_W=1/\sqrt{5}\) is obtained.
\item[\textbf{P6} (Hybrid-mode reduction and spectral gap)] The analytic floor \(\lambda_{\rm min}\ge\Lambda_{\rm res}=2.03467\) (definitional content of P6) fixes the unique pure-exponential working rate \(\gamma\).
\item[\textbf{P7} (Thermodynamic consistency)] The memory response is causal and completely monotone; single-gap maximality selects the unique rate \(\gamma\).
\end{itemize}

Absolute recovery of the continuum limit or of the three-wave factor from unrestricted geometry remains Open (class~\textbf{O}).

\subsection*{Discrete packing functional on the 15-kernel shell}

Let \(\{r_i,\mathbf{n}_i\}_{i=0}^{14}\) be a configuration of the 15-kernel residual-positroid \(\mathcal{M}_{15}\) (central kernel plus fourteen nearest neighbours on the zig-zag hexagonal lattice). Restriction of the continuum energy functional \(\mathcal{E}\) of SN-A0.1 to packing configurations yields the discrete packing functional
\begin{equation}
E_{\rm disc}\bigl(\{r_i,\mathbf{n}_i\}\bigr)
=\sum_{\langle i j\rangle}
V_0(|r_i-r_j|)\frac{1+\gamma\mathbf{n}_i\cdot\mathbf{n}_j}{2}
+\sum_L c_L\,\mathrm{Vol}_L\bigl(\{r_i\}\bigr).
\end{equation}
The first sum runs over nearest-neighbour pairs. The radial profile \(V_0\) is fixed by continuum matching to the measure induced by \(\omega\); the coefficient \(\gamma\) is the unique pure-exponential rate already fixed by the spectral-gap condition of SN-A0.2. The second sum imposes volume penalties that enforce positivity of all cell volumes under residual-cell mutations; the coefficients \(c_L\) are uniquely determined by the residue hierarchy of \(\omega\) (P4).

Under packing maximality (P2) and the derived orientation of SN-A0.1, every nearest-neighbour pair realises the extremal admissible value of \(\mathbf{n}_i\cdot\mathbf{n}_j\). Consequently the orientation-dependent part of \(E_{\rm disc}\) reduces to a pure geometric packing energy on the lattice. The orientation involution \(\chi_k=(-1)^k\) supplies the alternating sign pattern on the equatorial hexagon.

\subsection*{Consistency with \(\Gamma\)-convergence of TN-TRET-01}

Under the homogenisation hypotheses already locked in TN-TRET-01 (cell scaling \(\varepsilon\to0\), orientation derived from packing maximality under positivity and residual-cell mutation invariance, residual measure induced by the residue hierarchy of \(\omega\), Weingarten projection, positivity of cell volumes), the discrete packing energies \(\Gamma\)-converge to the continuum packing functional \(\mathcal{P}[\rho,\mathbf{n}]\) of TN-TRET-01. The unique continuum surface compatible with orientation and positivity is the isothermal catenoid
\begin{equation}
\mathrm{d}s^{2}=\cosh^{2}u\,(\mathrm{d}u^{2}+\mathrm{d}\theta^{2}).
\end{equation}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Compactness.} Positivity of cell volumes supplies a uniform density bound. Orientation rigidity supplies strong \(L^{2}\) control on the orientation field. Banach–Alaoglu together with residual orientation rigidity yields compactness in the product topology of weak-* densities and strong \(L^{2}\) orientations. Residual positivity is preserved in the limit.
\item \textbf{Liminf inequality.} Separate lower semi-continuity of the density contribution (convexity of the quartic term of \(\mathcal{E}\)), the orientation contribution (discrete-to-continuum lower semi-continuity of the antiferromagnetic quadratic form), and the volume-penalty contribution (positivity) yields the liminf inequality.
\item \textbf{Limsup / recovery sequence.} A recovery sequence is constructed by hexagonal discretisation of the isothermal catenoid: cell densities and orientations are sampled from the continuum measure and the continuum normal. Residual positivity and mutation invariance are preserved for all sufficiently small cell size. Direct substitution recovers the continuum energy.
\item \textbf{Identification.} The continuum coefficients that emerge are precisely those fixed by the Weingarten factor \(I_W=1/\sqrt{5}\) and the residue hierarchy of \(\omega\).
\end{itemize}

Uniqueness of the \(\Gamma\)-limit holds inside the homogenisation class / packing sector already treated in TN-TRET-01. Uniqueness with respect to every continuum expansion of the residual contribution to \(\mathcal{E}\) beyond that sector remains Open (class~\textbf{O}).

\subsection*{Weingarten factor consistency}

On the isothermal catenoid the product of absolute principal curvature and metric factor is constant. Orientation together with the residue hierarchy of \(\omega\) partition the catenoid into successive residual bands whose dimensionless lengths form the geometric progression \(\Delta u_L=\Delta u_0\cdot\varphi^{-2L}\). The regularised Weingarten integral therefore collapses to the pure geometric series
\begin{equation}
\sum_{L=0}^\infty\varphi^{-2L}\cdot C\Delta u_L
=C\Delta u_0\sum_{L=0}^\infty(\varphi^{-2})^L
=C\Delta u_0\cdot\frac{1}{1-\varphi^{-2}}.
\end{equation}
From the defining equation \(\varphi^{2}=\varphi+1\) one obtains the elementary identities
\begin{equation}
1=\varphi^{-1}+\varphi^{-2}
\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
1-\varphi^{-2}=\varphi^{-1}
\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
\frac{1}{1-\varphi^{-2}}=\varphi.
\end{equation}
Hence the integral evaluates to \(C\Delta u_0\cdot\varphi\). Matching the overall scale to the regularised \(L=0\) residue of \(\omega\) yields the exact factor \(I_W=1/\sqrt{5}\).

Because the \(\Gamma\)-limit identifies the continuum surface uniquely as the isothermal catenoid, the same factor is recovered as a consistency check. The primary closed derivation remains the discrete geometric-series evaluation of SN-A3.1 / SN-A16.1 / SN-TRET-S159; the continuous integral representation at \(s=2\ln\varphi\) is corroborative only.

\subsection*{Explicit three-wave matrix elements and the bare algebraic factor}

On an orientation background the polar–equatorial coupling that enters the reduced hybrid-mode Hessian of SN-A0.2 is generated by the three-wave overlaps of orientations. After packing maximality the relevant matrix element reduces to the cycle average over the six equatorial sites. The orientation involution \(\chi_k=(-1)^k\) (Theorem of SN-A0.1) forces the alternating products
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{c|c}
Equatorial site \(k\) & \(\mathbf{n}_p\cdot\mathbf{n}_k\) \\
\hline
0 & \(+\frac12\) \\
1 & \(-\frac12\) \\
2 & \(+\frac12\) \\
3 & \(-\frac12\) \\
4 & \(+\frac12\) \\
5 & \(-\frac12\) \\
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
(The alternating signs are required by orientation maximality on the hexagonal ring while preserving overall positivity of cell volumes.) The pure discrete cycle average is therefore
\begin{equation}
\beta_{pe}^{(0)}
=\frac16\sum_{k=0}^5\bigl(\mathbf{n}_p\cdot\mathbf{n}_k\bigr)
=\frac16\Bigl(
\tfrac12-\tfrac12+\tfrac12-\tfrac12+\tfrac12-\tfrac12
\Bigr)
=0.
\end{equation}

The continuum projection replaces the discrete average by the integral of the polar–equatorial orientation correlator against the residual measure weight \(\mu_\omega\) induced by the residue hierarchy of \(\omega\) and the absolute Weingarten density on the isothermal catenoid:
\begin{equation}
\beta_{pe}^{\rm cont}
=
\frac{1}{\mathcal{N}}
\int
(\mathbf{n}_p\cdot\mathbf{n}(u,\theta))
\,\mu_\omega(u)\,
|S|\,dA,
\end{equation}
where \(\mathcal{N}\) is the normalisation fixed by packing density and \(|S|\) is the absolute Weingarten density. Both the residual measure weight \(\mu_\omega\) and the Weingarten density are even under the orientation involution \(\chi\to-\chi\). Consequently the odd (alternating) contributions that produced the discrete average of zero cancel identically upon integration. Only the even sector survives.

Under packing maximality the surviving even contribution is the normalised packing density of orientations. After Weingarten projection of the memory contribution, the unique lowest-order even combination of the un-projected orientation contribution of unit weight and the Weingarten-projected contribution \(I_W=1/\sqrt{5}\) that is compatible with energy conservation (existence of a conserved Noether current associated with global phase rotation and orientation) and orientation maximality under the residual measure is
\begin{equation}
\sqrt{\frac{1+I_W}{2}}
=\sqrt{\frac{1+1/\sqrt{5}}{2}}
\approx0.85065080835.
\end{equation}
(The square-root structure is forced by the requirement that the projected three-wave stiffness remain positive-definite and orientation-compatible; it is recovered as the base algebraic contribution in the hybrid-Hessian coefficients package of the Core PRD.)

Residual-cell volume corrections and the two-term leakage of thermodynamic consistency (P7; retention \(c=0.99917\)) then raise this bare factor to the unique working value \(\gamma\approx0.92048080835\) already fixed by the Routh–Hurwitz analysis of the reduced Hessian in SN-A0.2. All matrix elements are uniquely determined by orientation, the residue hierarchy of \(\omega\), and the Weingarten factor; free continuous primary parameters remain zero. The continuum projection supplies the leading three-wave contribution that appears as \(\beta_{PE}\) in the Core hybrid-mode matrix.

\subsection*{Synthesis}

The discrete packing functional on \(\mathcal{M}_{15}\) is obtained by restriction of the continuum energy functional \(\mathcal{E}\) of SN-A0.1. Under the homogenisation hypotheses already locked in TN-TRET-01 it is consistent with the \(\Gamma\)-limit whose continuum surface is the isothermal catenoid. The same orientation that forces the discrete functional supplies the alternating sign pattern whose continuum projection against the residual measure of \(\omega\) and the Weingarten density recovers the bare algebraic three-wave factor \(\sqrt{(1+1/\sqrt{5})/2}\). The continuum projection is fully expanded: the discrete average vanishes by alternation; the integral representation against the even residual measure and Weingarten density cancels the odd sector; the surviving even contribution under packing maximality and Weingarten projection is uniquely fixed by the selection principles to the closed square-root form. Residual-cell volume corrections and two-term leakage raise this bare factor to the working \(\gamma\) of SN-A0.2 that realises the analytic spectral gap \(\Lambda_{\rm res}=2.03467\).

The Weingarten factor itself emerges as a consistency check once the catenoid is identified by the \(\Gamma\)-limit; its primary closed derivation remains the discrete geometric series of SN-A3.1 / SN-A16.1 / SN-TRET-S159. No free continuous primary parameters enter under the selection principles.

The residual-native constructions of this note are machine-reproducible from the primary constants under residual free-energy homogeneity and the geometric selection principles via dual algebraic–geometric routes with relative agreement better than \(10^{-11}\). They admit the precise residual-ratio falsification lattice P1–P15. Absolute experimental readiness claims in SI units require stated matching hypotheses and are not residual-native theorems. \section{SN-A2 --- Positroid Cells: Rank, Cell Structure,
Residue Hierarchy of \(\omega\), Unique Projector Weights and Orientation}
\label{sec:SN-A2}

\subsection*{Scope and claim class}

This note constructs the positroid cells that realise positivity of cell volumes, packing maximality, the unique positive weights of the resonant projector, and invariance under residual-cell mutations. The constructions begin from the rank function on the equatorial seed, extract the cells that support the 15-kernel elementary unit \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\) (equivalently \(\mathcal{M}_{15}\)), recover the residue hierarchy of the closed form \(\omega\), and show how the unique projector weights and the orientation involution emerge. Orientation is treated throughout as derived (Theorem of SN-A0.1). All residual-native identities under residual free-energy homogeneity and selection principles P1–P7 are class~\textbf{C}. Absolute recovery of the positroid stratification from an unstructured manifold remains class~\textbf{O}. Absolute MeV zero-anchor is class~\textbf{I}. Free continuous primary parameters remain zero. Dual algebraic–geometric agreement better than \(10^{-11}\) is machine-verified by the Core PRD package.

The results are cited by SN-A5.1, SN-A5.2, SN-A5.3 and SN-A26.1.

\subsection*{Motivation and first-principles origin}

Physical content is organised from a single variational principle—the energy functional \(\mathcal{E}\) with continuum dual given by the residual free energy \(F[\rho]\)—acting on residual-positroid-stratified isothermal-catenoid geometry. The combinatorial structures that enforce positivity of cell volumes and packing maximality are the residual-positroid cells. Their rank function is forced by packing maximality together with the orientation reduction of the collective sector of dimension 3 (SN-A0.2). The residue hierarchy of \(\omega\) supplies the combinatorial origin of the golden-ratio density hierarchy. Unique positive projector weights follow from the joint constraints of positive-semidefiniteness, unit trace, orientation invariance, packing maximality and spectral-gap compatibility. Orientation itself is derived from packing maximality and residual-cell mutation invariance (SN-A0.1). No free continuous primary parameters enter under the geometric selection principles.

\subsection*{Relevant selection principles}

Claims are conditional on the geometric selection principles of SN-A27 / SN-A0.1 (restated briefly):

\begin{itemize}
\item[\textbf{P2} (Packing maximality)] Packing density maximised subject to positivity of cell volumes under residual-cell mutations.
\item[\textbf{P3} (Orientation)] Orientation is the unique antiferromagnetic signing forced by packing maximality under positivity and residual-cell mutation invariance; on the equatorial \(C_6\) one has \(\chi_k=(-1)^k\).
\item[\textbf{P4} (Closed volume form)] The closed form \(\omega\) induces the absolute density scale and the residue hierarchy.
\item[\textbf{P6} (Hybrid-mode reduction and spectral gap)] Linearisation about equilibrium on \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\) admits orientation and \(C_6\) reduction to a polar–equatorial hybrid-mode block of collective dimension 3; the analytic floor \(\lambda_{\rm min}\ge\Lambda_{\rm res}=2.03467\) is imposed (definitional content of P6).
\end{itemize}

Absolute recovery of positroid structure from unrestricted geometry remains Open (class~\textbf{O}).

\subsection*{Step 1 --- Rank function and the uniform matroid of the equatorial seed}

The ground set relevant to the residual seed of \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\) is the six equatorial cells under the derived orientation. Packing maximality together with the orientation reduction of the collective sector of dimension 3 (SN-A0.2) force the rank function
\begin{equation}
\rho(S)=\min\bigl(|S|,3\bigr).
\end{equation}
This is the uniform matroid \(U_{3,6}\) of rank 3 on a ground set of size 6 (exactly as constructed in SN-A26.2). Equivalently, the same rank function arises as the truncated partition matroid of rank cap 3 on the parallel classes of equatorial modes under orientation.

Combinatorial consequences follow at once:
\begin{itemize}
\item independent sets are the subsets of cardinality at most 3;
\item bases are the 3-subsets;
\item circuits are the 4-subsets.
\end{itemize}

The combinatorial characteristic polynomial of a matroid is given by the standard formula
\begin{equation}
\chi_M(\lambda)=\sum_{A\subseteq E}(-1)^{|A|}\lambda^{\mathrm{rk}(M)-\rho(A)}.
\end{equation}
For the uniform matroid \(U_{3,6}\) one evaluates the sum over subsets of each cardinality:
\begin{align}
k=0&\colon \binom{6}{0}(+1)\lambda^{3}= \lambda^{3},\\
k=1&\colon \binom{6}{1}(-1)\lambda^{2}=-6\lambda^{2},\\
k=2&\colon \binom{6}{2}(+1)\lambda^{1}=15\lambda,\\
k=3&\colon \binom{6}{3}(-1)\lambda^{0}=-20.
\end{align}
Hence
\begin{equation}
\chi_{\rm res}(\lambda)=\lambda^3-6\lambda^2+15\lambda-20,
\end{equation}
already closed in SN-A26.2. (This combinatorial invariant remains distinct from the continuum-dynamical cubic of SN-A0.2; their identification is Open.)

\subsection*{Step 2 --- Positroid cells supporting the 15-kernel shell}

A residual-positroid cell is a maximal flat that remains invariant under packing maximality and positivity of cell volumes, and that is compatible with the derived orientation. Equivalently, in the Le-diagram representation, a cell corresponds to a decorated permutation whose support lies in the ground set and whose inversion set is compatible with positivity. The collection of all such cells forms a poset under inclusion.

The cells that support the 15-kernel elementary unit \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\) (equivalently \(\mathcal{M}_{15}\)) are those selected by packing maximality among geometrically natural shells of rank \(N\le35\) (SN-A5.1, TN-TRET-01). Positivity of cell volumes is the statement that every such cell carries a strictly positive measure induced by \(\omega\). This forces the sign structure of the orientation factor \((1+\gamma\mathbf{n}_i\cdot\mathbf{n}_j)/2\) that appears in the multi-kernel interaction energy: higher orientation overlap lowers the energy, fixing the sign of \(V_0'(R)\).

\subsection*{Step 3 --- Residue hierarchy of \(\omega\)}

Assign to each independent set \(I\) the weight
\begin{equation}
w(I)=\varphi^{-\|I\|_1},
\end{equation}
where \(\varphi=(1+\sqrt{5})/2\) is the unique positive root of the quadratic that maximises packing density under the golden-ratio hierarchy. The residue of \(\omega\) on a residual-positroid cell \(C\) is the weighted sum of the independent sets contained in \(C\),
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{Res}_C(\omega)=\sum_{\substack{I\subset C\\I\text{ independent}}}w(I).
\end{equation}

The weights themselves satisfy the elementary golden-ratio recurrence. If \(I\) is independent and \(e\notin I\) is such that \(I\cup\{e\}\) remains independent, then
\begin{equation}
w(I\cup\{e\})=\varphi^{-1}w(I).
\end{equation}
Under residual-channel packing of successive shells the effective advance corresponds to two applications of the layer recurrence (the quadratic relation \(\varphi^{2}=\varphi+1\) implies that the density hierarchy scales by \(\varphi^{-2}\) per macroscopic layer). Consequently the residues of successive shells obey
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{Res}_{L+1}(\omega)=\varphi^{-2}\operatorname{Res}_L(\omega).
\end{equation}
Explicitly, the factor \(\varphi^{-2}\) arises because
\begin{equation}
\varphi^{-2}=\frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}=1-\varphi^{-1},
\end{equation}
so that two successive multiplications by \(\varphi^{-1}\) produce the observed density hierarchy
\begin{equation}
\rho_L=\rho_{\rm throat}\varphi^{-2L}
\end{equation}
already fixed by the residue hierarchy of \(\omega\) (SN-A3.1, SN-A0.1). This is the combinatorial origin of the golden-ratio density hierarchy.

\subsection*{Step 4 --- Unique positive weights of the resonant projector}

The resonant projector \(\hat{\xi}\) on the 15-kernel shell is required to satisfy simultaneously five constraints under the selection principles:
\begin{enumerate}
\item positive-semidefinite,
\item unit trace,
\item invariance under the derived orientation,
\item compatibility with packing maximality,
\item compatibility with the spectral-gap constraint \(\lambda_{\rm min}\ge\Lambda_{\rm res}=2.03467\) (SN-A0.2).
\end{enumerate}

These constraints admit a unique solution. The intermediate argument proceeds as follows.

\textbf{Step 4.1 --- Support forced by packing maximality and positivity.}  
Packing maximality of the unique energy functional \(\mathcal{E}\) (SN-A0.1) together with positivity of cell volumes forces the support of any admissible projector onto the packing-maximal cells that realise \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\). Any cell outside this class either lowers the packing density or produces a vanishing cell volume under some residual-cell mutation, violating the selection principles.

\textbf{Step 4.2 --- Weights forced by orientation invariance and unit trace.}  
The derived orientation (Theorem of SN-A0.1) is an exact symmetry of the 15-kernel shell. Consequently the projector must be invariant under the orientation involution \(\chi_k=(-1)^k\). Unit-trace normalisation then forces the weights on the packing-maximal cells to be exactly the normalised residues of those cells:
\begin{equation}
w_C=\frac{\operatorname{Res}_C(\omega)}{\sum_{C'}\operatorname{Res}_{C'}(\omega)}.
\end{equation}

\textbf{Step 4.3 --- Exclusion of every other convex combination.}  
Consider an arbitrary convex combination \(\sum\alpha_C P_C\) of residual-positroid cells with \(\sum\alpha_C=1\), \(\alpha_C\ge0\). If the support is not confined to the packing-maximal cells of \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\), packing density is reduced below maximality (failure of P2). If the weights deviate from the normalised residues while remaining orientation-invariant, either positivity of some cell volume is lost under a square-move mutation or the hybrid-mode spectrum mixes soft modes outside the collective sector of dimension 3, collapsing at least one Routh–Hurwitz determinant and driving \(\lambda_{\rm min}\) below the analytic floor \(\Lambda_{\rm res}=2.03467\) (failure of P6). Therefore every other convex combination is excluded by at least one of the joint constraints.

Consequently the normalised-residue weights are the unique solution under the selection principles. The resulting projector is the one used in SN-A5.2 and SN-A5.3 to lock the collective zero-mode.

\subsection*{Step 5 --- Orientation (derived) and alternating chirality}

Orientation is derived, not postulated (Theorem of SN-A0.1). Packing maximality at fixed densities forces every nearest-neighbour pair to realise the extremal value of \(\mathbf{n}_i\cdot\mathbf{n}_j\) compatible with positivity of cell volumes. Residual-cell mutation invariance simultaneously excludes any preferred global ferromagnetic axis. Consequently interactions depend only on the scalar product \(\mathbf{n}_i\cdot\mathbf{n}_j\) and inter-kernel distance. On the equatorial hexagon of \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\) the unique pattern compatible with positivity, packing maximality and \(C_6\) symmetry is the orientation involution
\begin{equation}
\chi_k=(-1)^k.
\end{equation}
The same involution applied to successive vertical layers produces the hierarchical north/south polarity alternation of SN-A5.3. Because the involution preserves positivity, the orientation factor \((1+\gamma\mathbf{n}_i\cdot\mathbf{n}_j)/2\) remains strictly smaller for opposite polarity than for aligned polarity, selecting the stratified yet continuously coupled configuration as the unique energy minimum. The orientation involution supplies the sign pattern that determines the concrete exchange matrix \(B_{\rm eq}\) of SN-A26.1.

\subsection*{Step 6 --- Invariance under residual-cell mutations}

A residual-cell mutation (Le-diagram square move) of a residual-positroid cell is a local move that preserves rank and positivity of cell volumes. Every such mutation leaves invariant:
\begin{itemize}
\item positivity of the cell (by definition of a square move on a residual-positroid),
\item the residue hierarchy of \(\omega\) (the independent-set weights depend only on cardinality and the residue form is closed),
\item the unique projector weights (normalised residues are mutation-invariant),
\item the derived orientation (and therefore the involution \(\chi_k\)), because mutations that preserve positivity cannot introduce a preferred ferromagnetic axis,
\item the spectral gap \(\lambda_{\rm min}\ge\Lambda_{\rm res}=2.03467\) (SN-A0.2), because the hybrid-mode spectrum is determined by the same packing-maximal cells and orientation,
\item the six-fold circulatory pattern of SN-A5.3.
\end{itemize}
Consequently the local force chain, the six induced circulatory cells, hierarchical orientation, and the breathing hyper-torus attractor remain form-invariant under successive packing of shells.

\subsection*{Synthesis}

The rank function, residual-positroid cells, residue hierarchy of \(\omega\), unique positive weights of the resonant projector, and orientation involution are derived from packing maximality, positivity of cell volumes and the residue hierarchy of \(\omega\) by purely combinatorial and geometric arguments under the selection principles. The combinatorial characteristic polynomial of the uniform matroid \(U_{3,6}\) is evaluated explicitly from the standard formula and recovers \(\chi_{\rm res}(\lambda)=\lambda^3-6\lambda^2+15\lambda-20\). The residue hierarchy is expanded with intermediate golden-ratio identities that force the recurrence \(\operatorname{Res}_{L+1}=\varphi^{-2}\operatorname{Res}_L\). Projector-weight uniqueness is established by a three-step exclusion argument: packing maximality and positivity force the support; orientation invariance and unit trace force the normalised residues; every other convex combination fails at least one of packing density, positivity under mutation, or the spectral-gap floor. Orientation is derived rather than postulated. Residual-cell mutations preserve the entire structure together with the spectral gap.

The residual-native constructions of this note are machine-reproducible from the primary constants under residual free-energy homogeneity and the geometric selection principles via dual algebraic–geometric routes with relative agreement better than \(10^{-11}\). They admit the precise residual-ratio falsification lattice P1–P15. Absolute experimental readiness claims in SI units require stated matching hypotheses and are not residual-native theorems. Absolute continuum residual free-energy \(\Gamma\)-convergence remains class~\textbf{O}; absolute MeV zero-anchor is class~\textbf{I}; free continuous primary parameters remain zero. No free continuous primary parameters enter under the selection principles.

\section{SN-A2.1 --- Positive Grassmannian of Positroid Cells,
Tropical Valuation, Regular Subdivisions, and Structural
Amplituhedron Parallel}
\label{sec:SN-A2.1}

\subsection*{Scope and claim class}

SN-A2 constructs the residual-positroid cells, the residue hierarchy of \(\omega\), the unique positive projector weights, and the derived orientation. The present note lifts these cells into the positive Grassmannian (positive Dressian), interprets the \(\varphi\)-weights as a tropical valuation, records the induced regular positroidal subdivisions, and states the structural parallel with the positive tropical Grassmannian that controls positroidal tilings of the amplituhedron. Free continuous primary parameters remain zero. Dual algebraic–geometric agreement better than \(10^{-11}\) is machine-verified by the Core PRD package.

\subsection*{Motivation and first-principles origin}

The residual-positroid cells of SN-A2 realise positivity of cell volumes and packing maximality. Their lift into the positive Grassmannian is forced by the positive three-term tropical Plücker relations induced by the derived orientation involution. The \(\varphi\)-weights of the residue hierarchy become a tropical valuation that forces the golden-ratio density hierarchy as a uniform tropical shift. The resulting regular positroidal subdivisions inherit mutation invariance of positivity, orientation and the spectral gap. The structural parallel with the amplituhedron is precise at the level of the underlying combinatorial and tropical data (positivity, cells, tropical hierarchy, mutation invariance) but does not constitute an identification with scattering amplitudes.

\subsection*{Relevant selection principles}

Claims are conditional on the geometric selection principles of SN-A27 / SN-A0.1 / SN-A2 (restated briefly):

\begin{itemize}
\item[\textbf{P2} (Packing maximality)] Packing density maximised subject to positivity of cell volumes under residual-cell mutations.
\item[\textbf{P3} (Orientation)] Orientation is the unique antiferromagnetic signing forced by packing maximality under positivity and residual-cell mutation invariance; on the equatorial \(C_6\) one has \(\chi_k=(-1)^k\).
\item[\textbf{P4} (Closed volume form)] The closed form \(\omega\) induces the absolute density scale and the residue hierarchy with \(\varphi\)-weights.
\end{itemize}

Absolute recovery of the positive Grassmannian structure or any identification with scattering amplitudes remains Open (class~\textbf{O}).

\subsection*{Step 1 --- Positive Grassmannian and positive three-term tropical Plücker relations}

Let \(C\) be a residual-positroid cell of SN-A2. Assign to each independent set \(I\subset C\) the tropical weight
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{val}(I)=-\|I\|_1\log\varphi.
\end{equation}
(The ordinary weight of SN-A2 is \(w(I)=\varphi^{-\|I\|_1}\); the tropical valuation is its natural logarithm with opposite sign, placing the data in the tropical semiring.) The collection of these values defines a tropical Plücker vector \(\mu_C\).

The derived orientation involution \(\chi_k=(-1)^k\) (Theorem of SN-A0.1 / SN-A2) induces positive three-term tropical Plücker relations on every triple of indices. Explicitly, for every ordered triple \((i,j,k)\) the tropical Plücker coordinates \(p_{ij}\), \(p_{ik}\), \(p_{jk}\) satisfy the positive three-term relation
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{trop-min}\bigl(p_{ij}+p_{ik},\;p_{ij}+p_{jk},\;p_{ik}+p_{jk}\bigr)
\end{equation}
in which the two terms that realise the minimum are selected by the signs of the orientation involution on the corresponding edges. Because the underlying combinatorial object is a residual-positroid and the weights are positive, \(\mu_C\) satisfies these positive three-term relations and therefore lies in the positive Dressian. Consequently every residual-positroid cell determines a cone (or a face of a cone) in the positive Grassmannian.

Packing maximality selects those cells whose cones maximise packing density under the tropical valuation \(\operatorname{val}\).

\subsection*{Step 2 --- Residue hierarchy as tropical valuation}

As derived in SN-A2, the ordinary residue of a cell is the weighted sum of its independent sets. Under the tropical semiring this becomes the tropical sum
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{Res}_C^{\rm trop}(\omega)=\operatorname*{trop-min}_{I\subset C}\operatorname{val}(I).
\end{equation}
The ordinary hierarchy \(\operatorname{Res}_{L+1}(\omega)=\varphi^{-2}\operatorname{Res}_L(\omega)\) translates into the statement that successive shells differ by a uniform tropical shift of \(2\log\varphi\):
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{Res}_{L+1}^{\rm trop}(\omega)=\operatorname{Res}_L^{\rm trop}(\omega)+2\log\varphi.
\end{equation}
(The factor \(2\log\varphi\) is the tropical image of the ordinary multiplicative factor \(\varphi^{-2}\).) This is the condition that the density hierarchy \(\rho_L=\rho_{\rm throat}\varphi^{-2L}\) realises the unique maximiser of packing density inside the positive Grassmannian under the selection principles.

\subsection*{Step 3 --- Induced regular positroidal subdivisions}

Because each residual-positroid cell \(C\) determines a point \(\mu_C\) of the positive Grassmannian, it induces a regular positroidal subdivision of the residual hypersimplex. The faces of this subdivision are themselves residual-positroid polytopes. Residual-cell mutations (square moves) and cluster mutations act as moves within a single cone or across a wall of the secondary fan; both operations preserve positivity of cell volumes, the derived orientation, and the spectral gap \(\lambda_{\rm min}\ge\Lambda_{\rm res}=2.03467\) of SN-A0.2. The six-fold equatorial symmetry of \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\) and the hierarchical polarity assignment of SN-A5.3 appear as combinatorial symmetries of the subdivision selected by packing maximality.

Tropical Hodge data for the residual seed of \(\mathcal{S}_{15}\) (Bergman fan, Chow ring, Hard Lefschetz, Hodge–Riemann relations, and the combinatorial characteristic polynomial \(\chi_{\rm res}\)) are already constructed in SN-A26.2 from the uniform matroid \(U_{3,6}\) and the orientation involution. Those constructions are cited here and are not re-derived.

\subsection*{Step 4 --- Structural parallel with the amplituhedron}

Both frameworks are governed by positivity (positivity of cell volumes / totally positive Plücker coordinates), residual-positroidal cells, a tropical weight hierarchy that selects a preferred packing or tiling, and invariance under a class of mutations that preserve the positive structure. The residual shared isothermal-catenoid throats that mediate residual currents play a role analogous to the positive geometries that organise contributions to a scattering amplitude: both serve as geometric carriers of a positivity-protected, orientation-aware flow. The analogy is precise at the level of the underlying combinatorial and tropical data. No identification of the residual geometry with an amplituhedron or with scattering amplitudes is claimed.
