\section{SN-A93 --- Exact Residual Zig-Zag Packing Angles on $\mathcal{S}_{15}$}
\label{sec:SN-A93}
%==============================================================================

\subsection*{Scope and claim class}
This note derives the exact residual angles of the zig-zag hexagonal packing arrangement
on the 15-kernel coordination shell $\mathcal{S}_{15}$ from residual packing maximality,
AF $C_6$ geometry, equal residual nearest-neighbour centre-bond length, and the residual
aspect ratio $\sigma=\varphi^{-1}$ (unique positive root of the golden-ratio quadratic forced
by positivity of residual cell volumes; SN-A16.2). All residual-native angle identities are
class~\textbf{C}. Absolute recovery from unrestricted continuum geometry remains class~\textbf{O}.
Free continuous primary parameters remain zero. Absolute MeV zero-anchor remains Impossible.

\subsection*{Inputs already closed}
\begin{itemize}
\item AF $C_6$ from densest plane packing (SN-A79); equatorial angular pitch $2\pi/6$.
\item $\mathcal{S}_{15}$: central reference + 6 equatorial + 4 upper + 4 lower (SN-A5.1, A80, A87).
\item Aspect ratio $\sigma=\varphi^{-1}$ of the residual hyper-torus (SN-A16.2).
\item Weingarten factor $I_W=1/\sqrt{5}$ (primary discrete geometric series).
\item Chiral residue $\chi=\varphi^{-2}$.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Residual shell geometry}

\begin{definition}[Residual $\mathcal{S}_{15}$ zig-zag packing]
\label{def:A93-S15}
Place residual kernels of common residual nearest-neighbour scale $R>0$ as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Centre:} $\mathbf{r}_0=\mathbf{0}$.
\item \textbf{Equatorial $C_6$:}
\begin{equation}
\mathbf{r}_k^{\rm eq}
=R\bigl(\cos(k\pi/3),\,\sin(k\pi/3),\,0\bigr),
\qquad k=0,\ldots,5.
\end{equation}
Centre--equatorial and equatorial--equatorial residual distances both equal $R$, so the
equatorial pitch is exactly
\begin{equation}
\theta_{\rm eq}=\frac{2\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{3}\qquad(60^\circ).
\end{equation}
\item \textbf{Upper/lower residual rings ($4+4$):} four upper and four lower kernels at elevation
angle $\alpha$ from the equatorial plane and cylindrical radius $R\cos\alpha$, with common residual
centre-distance $R$:
\begin{equation}
\mathbf{r}_j^{\rm up/lo}
=
R\bigl(
\cos\alpha\cos\psi_j,\,
\cos\alpha\sin\psi_j,\,
\pm\sin\alpha
\bigr),
\quad
\psi_j=\psi_0+j\tfrac{\pi}{2}.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\subsection{Aspect ratio and exact elevation angle}

\begin{theorem}[Residual aspect ratio dual route]
\label{thm:A93-aspect}
The residual hyper-torus aspect ratio is
\begin{equation}
\sigma=\varphi^{-1}=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2},
\end{equation}
with dual algebraic agreement better than $10^{-11}$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textbf{Route A.}] Positivity of residual cell volumes selects the unique positive root of
\begin{equation}
r^{2}+r-1=0
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
r=\frac{-1+\sqrt{5}}{2}=\varphi^{-1}.
\end{equation}
\item[\textbf{Route B.}] Golden-ratio identity with residual chiral residue
\begin{equation}
\sigma=1-\chi=1-\varphi^{-2}=\varphi^{-1}.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Route~A is residual packing stationarity of SN-A16.2: residual cell-volume positivity on the closed
force balance of the equatorial 7-kernel hyper-torus forces the golden quadratic; the negative root is
discarded by positivity. Route~B uses $\chi=\varphi^{-2}$ and $1-\varphi^{-2}=\varphi^{-1}$. Both
evaluate to $(\sqrt{5}-1)/2$. Certificate: \texttt{A93\_zigzag\_packing\_angles\_certificate.json}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact residual zig-zag elevation angle]
\label{thm:A93-alpha}
Under equal residual centre-bond length $R$ and residual aspect ratio $\sigma=\varphi^{-1}$ identifying
the vertical scale of elevated residual bonds,
\begin{equation}
\sin\alpha=\varphi^{-1},
\qquad
\cos\alpha=\varphi^{-1/2},
\qquad
\tan\alpha=\varphi^{-1/2},
\end{equation}
so
\begin{equation}
\alpha
=\arcsin(\varphi^{-1})
=\arccos(\varphi^{-1/2})
=\arctan(\varphi^{-1/2})
\approx 38.172707627012^\circ.
\end{equation}
The residual polar angle from the positive $z$-axis is
\begin{equation}
\beta=\arccos(\varphi^{-1})=\frac{\pi}{2}-\alpha
\approx 51.827292372988^\circ.
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Full intermediate algebra]
Equal residual centre-bond length places every elevated kernel on the residual sphere of radius $R$.
The residual aspect ratio identifies the vertical residual scale with
\begin{equation}
\frac{h}{R}=\sigma=\varphi^{-1}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\sin\alpha=\varphi^{-1}.
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
\cos\alpha
=\sqrt{1-\sin^{2}\alpha}
=\sqrt{1-\varphi^{-2}}
=\sqrt{\varphi^{-1}}
=\varphi^{-1/2},
\end{equation}
where $1-\varphi^{-2}=\varphi^{-1}$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:A93-aspect}, Route~B). Hence
\begin{equation}
\tan\alpha
=\frac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha}
=\frac{\varphi^{-1}}{\varphi^{-1/2}}
=\varphi^{-1/2}.
\end{equation}
Complementarity $\beta=\pi/2-\alpha$ is immediate. No free continuous primary parameter enters.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Equatorial pitch]
\label{cor:A93-eq}
$\theta_{\rm eq}=\pi/3$ ($60^\circ$), forced by AF $C_6$ densest-plane packing together with equal residual
centre and equatorial bond lengths.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Geometry-fixed residual Weingarten weights]
\label{thm:A93-weights}
\begin{align}
T_6&=\frac{I_W}{6}=\frac{1}{6\sqrt{5}},\\
w_{\rm rad}&=I_W\cos\alpha=I_W\,\varphi^{-1/2},\\
w_{\rm vert}&=I_W\sin\alpha=I_W\,\varphi^{-1}.
\end{align}
These residual geometric weights replace free memory/packing fit coefficients in residual geometric
sectors of the memory-projected AF $C_6$ operator (SN-A85) without flipping \texttt{absolute\_closed}.
\end{theorem}

\section{SN-A97 --- Unique Residual Memory Amplitude
$I_W^{2}/\gamma=I_W/(\gamma\sqrt{5})$}
\label{sec:SN-A97}

\begin{theorem}[Residual memory amplitude identity]
\label{thm:A97-id}
\begin{equation}
\frac{I_W}{\gamma\sqrt{5}}
=
\frac{I_W^{2}}{\gamma},
\end{equation}
exact, because $I_W=1/\sqrt{5}$ implies $I_W/\sqrt{5}=I_W^{2}$. Dual-route evaluation of $I_W$ as
$1/\sqrt{5}$ and $\sqrt{5}/5$ agrees to better than $10^{-11}$. At $\gamma_{\rm res}$,
\begin{equation}
a_{\rm mem}(\gamma_{\rm res})
=\frac{I_W^{2}}{\gamma_{\rm res}}
\approx 0.217277751133680.
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$I_W=1/\sqrt{5}$ (primary discrete geometric series). Then $I_W/\sqrt{5}=1/5=I_W^{2}$. Multiply by
$1/\gamma$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Residual-native uniqueness under A7/A8/Weingarten]
\label{thm:A97-unique}
Under residual pure-exponential memory $K(t)=\gamma e^{-\gamma t}$ (residual axiom A8), residual
Weingarten projection with exact factor $I_W$, and residual free-energy force-chain structure
(memory residual force $\propto I_W\cdot(K*\rho)$), the residual dimensionless memory amplitude in
residual units is uniquely $a_{\rm mem}(\gamma)=I_W^{2}/\gamma$. No free continuous residual primary
parameter $K_0$ remains once residual Weingarten residual scale is identified with $I_W$. Absolute
recovery from unrestricted continuum geometry without residual Weingarten structure remains Open.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Residual axiom A8 fixes the residual pure-exponential class. Residual Weingarten regularisation fixes
$I_W=1/\sqrt{5}$. Residual force-chain projection multiplies residual memory convolution by $I_W$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact residual polar Rayleigh quotient]
\label{thm:A109-Rp}

\begin{proof}[Full intermediate algebra]
Residual polar mode $\mathbf{v}_{p}=e_{0}$ has residual support only at residual centre.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Residual diagonal residual mass: $H_{00}$ receives residual site mass $\kappa=1+\gamma I_W$.
\item Residual centre--equatorial and residual centre--capacity residual hops contribute residual
off-diagonal entries $H_{0j}=-t$ but residual Rayleigh $\mathbf{v}_{p}^{\mathsf T}H\mathbf{v}_{p}$

\item Residual packing projector: $(P)_{00}=1-1/15=14/15$, so residual packing contributes
$S_{\rm pack}\cdot 14/15$.
\item Residual memory acts only on residual equatorial block: zero residual contribution to residual
polar.
\item Residual capacity residual dual mass $S_{\rm res}$ acts only on residual capacity sites.
\end{enumerate}
Hence $R_{p}=\kappa+S_{\rm pack}\cdot 14/15$. Numerical evaluation at $\gamma_{\rm res}$ yields
$1.7986020150409407$, matching residual full residual matrix projection to absolute error

\begin{theorem}[Exact residual equatorial AF Rayleigh quotient]
\label{thm:A109-Re}
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A109-Re}
R_{e}
:=
\mathbf{v}_{e}^{\mathsf T}H^{\rm S15}\mathbf{v}_{e}
=

+
2t
+
7\,a_{\rm mem}

\begin{proof}[Full intermediate algebra]
Write residual equatorial AF components $v_{k}=(-1)^{k}/\sqrt{6}$ on residual sites $1,\ldots,6$
and zero elsewhere.

\textbf{(i) Residual diagonal $\kappa$.}
$\sum_{k}v_{k}^{2}\kappa=\kappa$.

\textbf{(ii) Residual equatorial ring hops.}
Residual ring edges $H_{k,k+1}=-t$ (indices mod $6$). Residual AF neighbour products:
\begin{equation}
v_{k}v_{k+1}
=
\frac{(-1)^{k}(-1)^{k+1}}{6}
=
-\frac{1}{6}.
\end{equation}
Residual Rayleigh contribution of residual off-diagonal residual ring:
\begin{equation}
\sum_{i\neq j}v_{i}H_{ij}v_{j}
=
2\sum_{\text{edges}}(-t)\Bigl(-\frac{1}{6}\Bigr)
=
2\cdot 6\cdot\frac{t}{6}
=
2t.
\end{equation}

\textbf{(iii) Residual memory.}
Residual memory operator on residual equatorial block:
$H^{\rm mem}_{ab}=a_{\rm mem}\bigl(\chi_{a}\chi_{b}+\delta_{ab}\bigr)$ with
$\chi_{k}=(-1)^{k}$. Then
\begin{align}
\mathbf{v}_{e}^{\mathsf T}H^{\rm mem}\mathbf{v}_{e}
&=
a_{\rm mem}
\Biggl(
\Bigl(\sum_{k=0}^{5}\chi_{k}v_{k}\Bigr)^{2}
+
\sum_{k=0}^{5}v_{k}^{2}
\Biggr)
\\
&=
a_{\rm mem}
\Biggl(
\Bigl(\sum_{k=0}^{5}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\Bigr)^{2}
+
1
\Biggr)
=
a_{\rm mem}\bigl(6+1\bigr)
=
7\,a_{\rm mem},
\end{align}
since $\chi_{k}v_{k}=(-1)^{k}\cdot(-1)^{k}/\sqrt{6}=1/\sqrt{6}$.

\textbf{(iv) Residual packing.}
$\sum_{i}v_{i}=0$ (residual AF sum), so

$\Lambda_{\rm res}$ \textbf{FALSE}; absolute $H_s$ uniqueness \textbf{OPEN}. Free continuous
primary parameters remain zero.

\begin{definition}[Nine sector Hessian operators]
\label{def:A113-Hs}
Order sites as centre $e_0$, equatorial $e_1,\ldots,e_6$, capacity $e_7,\ldots,e_{14}$.
With hop $t=t(\gamma)$, site mass $\kappa=\kappa(\gamma)$, memory $a_{\rm mem}=I_W^{2}/\gamma$,
packing projector $P=\mathbb{I}-\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}/15$, AF signs
$\chi_k=(-1)^k$ on the equator, and eq--capacity distances $d_{kj}$:
\begin{align}
(H_{\rm kin})_{ij} &= \kappa\,\delta_{ij},\\
(H_{\rm int})_{ij} &= \text{geometric hops: }{-t}\text{ on centre/eq/ring edges;}
\quad {-t}\,e^{-(d-1)^{2}}\text{ on throats }d<1.2;\\
&\qquad {-t}\cos\alpha\text{ on capacity rings; }\ {-t}\sin\alpha\text{ on vertical capacity pairs},\\
(H_W)_{ij} &= I_W^{2}\,\delta_{ij},\\
(H_{\rm mem})_{ab} &= a_{\rm mem}(\chi_a\chi_b+\delta_{ab})\quad\text{(equatorial block)},\\
(H_{\rm ori})_{ab} &= (I_W/6)\,\chi_a\chi_b\quad\text{(equatorial block)},\\
H_{\rm pack} &= S_{\rm pack}\,P,\\
(H_{\rm dual})_{ii} &= S_{\rm res}\quad(i\in\{7,\ldots,14\}),\\
H_{\rm leak} &= \eta_0\,\mathbb{I}+\text{throat discrete-gradient form at }\eta_{\rm leak}(1),\\
(H_{\rm boundary})_{ii} &= I_W\chi/6\quad(i\in\{7,\ldots,14\}).
\end{align}
Each operator is symmetrized: $H_s\leftarrow\frac12(H_s+H_s^{\mathsf T})$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Structural reconstruction of hybrid $H^{\rm S15}$]
\label{thm:A113-recon}
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A113-recon}
H^{\rm S15} = H_{\rm kin}+H_{\rm int}+H_{\rm mem}+H_{\rm pack}+H_{\rm dual}.
\end{equation}
Frobenius reconstruction error is identically zero (machine abs.\ err.\ $<10^{-15}$).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Full intermediate ledger]
\textbf{Step 1 (kinetic).}
Diagonal site mass of $H^{\rm S15}$ is $\kappa$ on every site: this is $H_{\rm kin}$.

\textbf{Step 2 (interaction hops).}
Centre--eq hops $-t$, equatorial ring hops $-t$, centre--capacity hops $-t$,
eq--capacity throats $-t\,e^{-(d-1)^{2}}$ ($d<1.2$), capacity ring hops $-t\cos\alpha$,
and vertical capacity pairs $-t\sin\alpha$ exhaust the support of $H_{\rm int}$.

\textbf{Step 3 (memory).}
Equatorial AF memory block $a_{\rm mem}(\chi\chi^{\mathsf T}+\mathbb{I}_6)$ is $H_{\rm mem}$.
Polar and capacity blocks receive zero memory mass.

\textbf{Step 4 (packing).} $S_{\rm pack}P$ is $H_{\rm pack}$.

\textbf{Step 5 (dual).} Capacity dual mass $S_{\rm res}$ on sites $7,\ldots,14$ is $H_{\rm dual}$.

\textbf{Step 6 (absent from structural hybrid).}
$H_W$, $H_{\rm ori}$, $H_{\rm leak}$, $H_{\rm boundary}$ do not enter $H^{\rm S15}$; they appear
only in the free-energy weight average of Theorem~\ref{thm:A113-weighted}.

Summing Steps 1--5 recovers $H^{\rm S15}$ entrywise.
Certificate: \texttt{A113\_sector\_hessian\_operators\_certificate.json},
field \texttt{structural\_reconstruction.frobenius\_error}$=0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Dual-route operator identities]
\label{thm:A113-dual-ops}
Absolute error $<10^{-11}$ on each:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H_{\rm pack}=S_{\rm pack}P$ (Frobenius error $0$).
\item $(H_{\rm dual})_{ii}=S_{\rm res}$ on capacity sites.
\item $(H_{\rm boundary})_{ii}=I_W\chi/6$ on capacity sites.
\item $(H_W)_{00}=I_W^{2}=1/5$.
\item $(H_{\rm kin})_{00}=\kappa(\gamma_{\rm res})$.
\item $\mathbf{v}_{e}^{\mathsf T}H_{\rm mem}\mathbf{v}_{e}=7\,a_{\rm mem}$
(AF equatorial mode $\mathbf{v}_{e}$ of SN-A109).
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Weighted free-energy Hessian vs package floor]
\label{thm:A113-weighted}

\section{SN-A114 --- Capacity Virtual Corrections beyond Pure $2\times2$}
\label{sec:SN-A114}
%==============================================================================

\subsection*{Scope and claim class}
Reduce the full $\mathcal{S}_{15}$ hybrid onto the polar--equatorial PE block by exact
Schur complement over the capacity block, obtaining capacity virtual corrections to the
pure $2\times2$ hybrid of SN-A109. Test whether the effective hybrid floor moves toward
package $\Lambda_{\rm res}$ without free coefficients. Claim: Schur algebra \textbf{C};
equality with $\Lambda_{\rm res}$ \textbf{FALSE}; closer-to-$\Lambda$ claim \textbf{FALSE}
(proved). Absolute unrestricted capacity reduction \textbf{OPEN}.

\begin{definition}[PE/capacity partition]
\label{def:A114-blocks}
Reorder sites as PE $=\{0,1,\ldots,6\}$ (dim $7$) and capacity $C=\{7,\ldots,14\}$ (dim $8$).
Partition $H^{\rm S15}$ as
\begin{equation}
H^{\rm S15}
= \begin{pmatrix} H_{\rm PE} & H_{\rm PC}\\ H_{\rm CP} & H_{\rm CC}\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact capacity Schur complement]
\label{thm:A114-Schur}
Assuming $H_{\rm CC}$ invertible (verified: $\lambda_{\min}(H_{\rm CC})>0$,
$\mathrm{cond}(H_{\rm CC})<\infty$), the effective PE Hessian is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A114-Heff}
H_{\rm eff}
:=
H_{\rm PE}
-
H_{\rm PC}\,H_{\rm CC}^{-1}\,H_{\rm CP}.
\end{equation}
Projecting onto polar mode $\mathbf{v}_p=e_0$ and AF equatorial mode
$\mathbf{v}_e=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\sum_{k=0}^{5}(-1)^k e_{1+k}$ yields the effective hybrid
$2\times2$
\begin{equation}
H^{(2)}_{\rm eff}
= \begin{pmatrix}
R_p^{\rm eff} & \delta^{\rm eff}\\
\delta^{\rm eff} & R_e^{\rm eff}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\delta^{\rm eff}\sim 10^{-20}.
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Full intermediate algebra]
\textbf{Step 1.} Form $H^{\rm S15}$ at $\gamma=\gamma_{\rm res}$ with A93 geometry
(exact $\sin\alpha=\varphi^{-1}$, $\cos\alpha=\varphi^{-1/2}$).

\textbf{Step 2.} Invert $H_{\rm CC}$ by dense LU; mean diagonal
$\overline{(H_{\rm CC})_{ii}}$ is used only for second-order scale estimates.

\textbf{Step 3.} Compute $H_{\rm eff}$ by \eqref{eq:A114-Heff}; symmetrize.

\textbf{Step 4.} Bare PE Rayleigh (no capacity virtual):
\begin{align}
R_p^{\rm bare}
&= \mathbf{v}_p^{\mathsf T}H_{\rm PE}\mathbf{v}_p
= 1.7986020150409407
= R_p^{\rm A109},\\
R_e^{\rm bare}
&= \mathbf{v}_e^{\mathsf T}H_{\rm PE}\mathbf{v}_e
= 3.426704784851704
= R_e^{\rm A109},\\
\delta^{\rm bare}
&= \mathbf{v}_p^{\mathsf T}H_{\rm PE}\mathbf{v}_e
\sim 10^{-18}.
\end{align}
Agreement with SN-A109 closed forms
$R_p=\kappa+S_{\rm pack}\cdot 14/15$ and
$R_e=\kappa+2t+7a_{\rm mem}+S_{\rm pack}$ is absolute error $<10^{-15}$.

\textbf{Step 5.} Effective Rayleigh after Schur:
\begin{align}
R_p^{\rm eff} &= 1.7768032808300727,\\
R_e^{\rm eff} &= 3.4266967515188003,\\
\delta^{\rm eff} &\sim 10^{-20}.
\end{align}
Virtual shifts:
\begin{align}
\Delta R_p &:= R_p^{\rm eff}-R_p^{\rm bare} = -0.021798734210868087,\\
\Delta R_e &:= R_e^{\rm eff}-R_e^{\rm bare} = -8.0333329037785\times 10^{-6}.
\end{align}
AF cancellation keeps off-diagonals at machine zero (SN-A109 analytic vanishing persists).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Capacity virtual does not recover package $\Lambda_{\rm res}$]
\label{thm:A114-vs-Lambda}
At package locks, with zero free coefficients:
\begin{align}
\lambda_{\min}(H^{(2)}_{\rm bare}) &= R_p^{\rm bare} = 1.7986020150409407,\\
\lambda_{\min}(H^{(2)}_{\rm eff}) &= R_p^{\rm eff} = 1.7768032808300727,\\
\lambda_{\min}(H^{\rm S15}) &= 1.3139932900162188,\\
\Lambda_{\rm res} &= 2.03467.
\end{align}
Gaps to package:
\begin{align}
|\lambda_{\min}(H^{(2)}_{\rm bare})-\Lambda_{\rm res}| &= 0.23606798495905945,\\
|\lambda_{\min}(H^{(2)}_{\rm eff})-\Lambda_{\rm res}| &= 0.25786671916992754.
\end{align}
Thus capacity virtual \textbf{increases} the gap to $\Lambda_{\rm res}$
(does not move closer). Equality at dual-route $10^{-11}$ is \textbf{FALSE}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $H^{(2)}$ is diagonal in the polar/eq AF basis (off-diag $<10^{-18}$),
$\lambda_{\min}=\min(R_p,R_e)=R_p$. Direct absolute comparison to package
$\Lambda_{\rm res}$ yields the gaps above. Effective gap exceeds bare gap, so the
``moves closer'' claim is FALSIFIED.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Second-order virtual scale]
Centre couples to eight capacity sites with hop $t$. Second-order polar estimate
$\Delta R_p^{\rm est}=-8t^{2}/\overline{(H_{\rm CC})_{ii}}$ gives
$-0.006493185609071946$, absolute error $0.0153$ vs exact $\Delta R_p$.
Throat count on eq--capacity contacts: $16$. Second-order estimates are diagnostic only;
the exact result is the Schur complement.
\end{remark}

\subsection*{Status (A114)}
Schur capacity virtual: C. Effective hybrid $=\Lambda_{\rm res}$: FALSE.
Closer to $\Lambda_{\rm res}$: FALSE (proved). \texttt{absolute\_closed}=false.

density and compare discrete $H^{\rm S15}$ spectrum to continuum gap estimates. Claim:
$\varepsilon$ dual-route and $\Gamma$-mask EL PDE \textbf{C}; absolute unrestricted continuum
series \textbf{OPEN}; discrete $\lambda_{\min}=\Lambda_{\rm res}$ \textbf{FALSE}.

\label{def:A116-eps}

&= \frac{\gamma}{2\sqrt{\Lambda_{\rm res}}} = 0.3226545186044022,\\
\varepsilon_W
&= \frac{I_W}{\sqrt{\Lambda_{\rm res}}} = 0.3135219899435783,\\
\varepsilon_\chi
&= \chi = 0.38196601125010515,\\

All four dual-route twins agree to absolute error $<10^{-15}$. Moreover

R_6
= \frac{(\max\varepsilon)^{7}}{1-\max\varepsilon}
= 0.0019193787254996315
\end{equation}
is finite (SN-A110).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Residual $\Gamma$-mask linearized EL PDE]
\label{thm:A116-EL}
Under residual $\Gamma$-mask, the linearized free-energy Euler--Lagrange dynamics for density
fluctuation $u$ is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A116-EL}
\varepsilon_{\rm damp}\,\partial_t u
= \varepsilon_W\,\Delta_W u
- \varepsilon_\chi\,\chi_{\rm mask}\,u
- \varepsilon_P\,P_{\rm pack}\,u
+ \mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{2}),
\end{equation}
where $\Delta_W$ is the residual Weingarten Laplacian, $\chi_{\rm mask}$ the residual chiral
mask, and $P_{\rm pack}$ the residual packing projector. The discrete realization of the
spatial operator on $\mathcal{S}_{15}$ is the structural hybrid $H^{\rm S15}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Full intermediate derivation]
\textbf{Step 1 (free-energy second variation).}
Residual free energy $\mathcal{E}$ of SN-A68/A108 has second variation
$\delta^{2}\mathcal{E}=\sum_s w_s\delta^{2}\mathcal{E}_s$. Continuum reduction under
$\Gamma$-mask expands each sector contribution in the dual-route scales of
Definition~\ref{def:A116-eps}.

\textbf{Step 2 (damping).}
Underdamped hybrid oscillator at floor $\Lambda_{\rm res}$ contributes residual time-scale
$\varepsilon_{\rm damp}=\gamma/(2\sqrt{\Lambda_{\rm res}})$ (dual-route closed form).

\textbf{Step 3 (Weingarten diffusion).}
Isothermal-catenoid Weingarten geometry contributes $\varepsilon_W\Delta_W$ with
$\varepsilon_W=I_W/\sqrt{\Lambda_{\rm res}}$.

\textbf{Step 4 (chiral mask).}
Chiral residue enters as multiplicative mask $\varepsilon_\chi=\chi$.

\textbf{Step 5 (packing).}
Packing projector contributes $\varepsilon_P P_{\rm pack}$ with
$\varepsilon_P=1/(1+\Lambda_{\rm res})$.

\textbf{Step 6 (higher order).}
Remainder series after linearization is controlled by $R_6$ (SN-A110 majorant); absolute
unrestricted continuum series without mask remains OPEN.

\textbf{Step 7 (discrete spectrum).}
On $\mathcal{S}_{15}$, spatial operator $\leftrightarrow H^{\rm S15}$ yields
\begin{align}
\lambda_{\min}(H^{\rm S15}) &= 1.3139932900162188,\\
\lambda_{\max}(H^{\rm S15}) &= 3.426715447311671,\\
\mathbf{v}_p^{\mathsf T}H^{\rm S15}\mathbf{v}_p &= 1.7986020150409407,\\
\mathbf{v}_e^{\mathsf T}H^{\rm S15}\mathbf{v}_e &= 3.4267047848517045,\\
\mathbf{v}_c^{\mathsf T}H^{\rm S15}\mathbf{v}_c &= 2.062399437438541.
\end{align}
Continuum gap majorants:
\begin{align}
\Lambda_{\rm res}(1-\max\varepsilon) &= 1.2574952158897488,\\
\Lambda_{\rm res}(1+\max\varepsilon) &= 2.8118447841102516,\\
L_{\rm cont}^{\rm est}
&= \Lambda_{\rm res}(1-\varepsilon_P)-\varepsilon_W I_W
= 1.2239838249566568.
\end{align}
$|L_{\rm cont}^{\rm est}-\lambda_{\min}(H^{\rm S15})|\approx 0.090$; discrete
$\lambda_{\min}\neq\Lambda_{\rm res}$ at $10^{-11}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Honesty on absolute continuum series]
All $\varepsilon$ coefficients use package $\Lambda_{\rm res}$ or dual-route geometry.
Equation~\eqref{eq:A116-EL} is residual-native under $\Gamma$-mask. Absolute continuum
series without residual seed remains OPEN (no flip of \texttt{absolute\_closed}).
\end{remark}

$\varepsilon$ dual-route: C. $\Gamma$-mask EL PDE: C. Absolute continuum series: OPEN.

\begin{theorem}[Fundamental packing-defect identities]
\label{thm:A122-fund}
The following hold with absolute error $<10^{-15}$ (dual-route tol $10^{-11}$):
\begin{enumerate}
\item $1-\chi=\sin\alpha=\varphi^{-1}$.
\item $R_{\rm nat}=I_W\sin\alpha\,\chi^{6}=I_W\,R_{6,\chi}$.
\item $c_{\rm nat}=1-R_{\rm nat}=1-I_W\sin\alpha\,\chi^{6}$.
\item $\Lambda_{\rm nat}(\gamma)-\bigl(\lambda_{\min}^{C_6}(\gamma)+S_{\rm pack}+I_W\sin\alpha\bigr)=R_{\rm nat}$
identically in $\gamma$.
\item $1/(1+\varphi)=\chi$ (golden projector identity).
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Full intermediate ledger]
\textbf{(1).}
$\chi=\varphi^{-2}$ and $\varphi^{2}=\varphi+1$, so
$1-\chi=1-\varphi^{-2}=(\varphi^{2}-1)/\varphi^{2}=\varphi/\varphi^{2}=\varphi^{-1}=\sin\alpha$.

\textbf{(2).}
$R_{6,\chi}=\chi^{7}/(1-\chi)=\chi^{7}/\sin\alpha$.
Thus $I_W R_{6,\chi}=I_W\chi^{7}/\sin\alpha$.
Also $I_W\sin\alpha\,\chi^{6}=I_W\chi^{6}\sin\alpha$.
Equality iff $\sin^{2}\alpha=\chi$.
But $\sin\alpha=\varphi^{-1}$ so $\sin^{2}\alpha=\varphi^{-2}=\chi$. Done.

\textbf{(3).} Immediate from Definition~\ref{def:A122-nat} and (2).

\textbf{(4).} By definition of $\Lambda_{\rm nat}$.

\textbf{(5).} $1+\varphi=\varphi^{2}$, hence $1/(1+\varphi)=\varphi^{-2}=\chi$.

Certificate: \texttt{MASTER\_A122\_A127\_certificate.json}, fields
\texttt{dual\_route\_nat}.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{Scope and claim class}

%------------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Definitions: notations, presentations, screws}
%------------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Hermann--Mauguin $\leftrightarrow$ Schoenflies isomorphism for hexagonal family]
\label{def:A146-HM-Schoenflies}
The following table identifies the abstract finite subgroups of $O(3)$ that leave a hexagonal
lattice invariant and contain an element of order $6$. The correspondence is the unique
(up to conjugacy in $O(3)$) isomorphism of groups that preserves the rotational order of the
principal axis and the geometric action on the lattice vectors of the hexagonal Bravais lattice.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llll@{}}
\toprule
Schoenflies & Hermann--Mauguin & Order & Standard presentation / generators \\
\midrule
$C_6$ & $6$ & $6$ & $\langle r\mid r^6=1\rangle$ \\
$C_{6h}$ & $6/m$ & $12$ & $\langle r,\sigma_h\mid r^6=\sigma_h^2=1,\;\sigma_h r\sigma_h^{-1}=r^{-1}\rangle$ \\
$C_{6v}$ & $6mm$ & $12$ & $\langle r,\sigma_v\mid r^6=\sigma_v^2=1,\;\sigma_v r\sigma_v^{-1}=r^{-1}\rangle$ \\
$D_6$ & $622$ & $12$ & $\langle r,s\mid r^6=s^2=1,\;srs^{-1}=r^{-1}\rangle$ \\
$D_{3h}$ & $\overline{6}m2$ & $12$ & (standard generators of order-$3$ rotation + mirrors) \\
$D_{6h}$ & $6/mmm$ & $24$ & $D_6\times\langle i\rangle$ (central inversion) or
$\langle r,s,\sigma_h\rangle$ with full relations \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The isomorphism is bijective on the hexagonal family of the $32$ crystallographic point groups
and is recorded in International Tables for Crystallography, Volume A.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Screw axis $6_3$]
\label{def:A146-63}
Let $\ell$ be a directed axis parallel to a lattice vector of length $c$. The screw isometry $6_3$
is the Euclidean isometry
\[
6_3:(x,y,z)\mapsto\bigl(x\cos\tfrac{\pi}{3}-y\sin\tfrac{\pi}{3},\;
x\sin\tfrac{\pi}{3}+y\cos\tfrac{\pi}{3},\;z+\tfrac{c}{2}\bigr).
\]
It belongs to the infinite discrete group of isometries of the hexagonal lattice. The pure
rotational part of its powers generates a cyclic group of order $6$. Explicitly:
\begin{align*}
(6_3)^2 &= 3_1\quad\text{(or $3_2$ according to orientation)},\\
(6_3)^3 &= 2_1,\\
(6_3)^6 &= T_{3c}\quad\text{(pure translation by $3c$)}.
\end{align*}
In the space group $P6_3/mmc$ (graphite) the $6_3$ axes occupy the centres of the hexagonal
prisms and are compatible with AB bilayer stacking.
\end{definition}

%------------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Hierarchy and maximality}
%------------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{theorem}[Holohedry maximality of $D_{6h}$]
\label{thm:A146-holohedry}
Let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ be a hexagonal Bravais lattice (or the $2$-dimensional hexagonal
lattice for layer groups). Let $G$ be any finite subgroup of $O(3)$ that leaves $\Lambda$
invariant and contains an element of rotational order $6$. Then $G$ is conjugate in $O(3)$
to a subgroup of the hexagonal holohedry $D_{6h}\simeq 6/mmm$ of order $24$. In particular,
the unique maximal crystallographic point group containing a principal $C_6$ is $D_{6h}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By the crystallographic restriction theorem the only possible finite rotational orders compatible
with a lattice are $1,2,3,4,6$. The complete classification of finite subgroups of $O(3)$ consists
of the cyclic groups $C_n$, the dihedral groups $D_n$, the polyhedral groups $A_4$, $S_4$, $A_5$
and their products with the central inversion $\{1,i\}$. Only those subgroups that preserve a
lattice appear among the $32$ crystallographic point groups.

Suppose $G$ contains a rotation $r$ of order $6$. Then the axis of $r$ must be a lattice direction
(otherwise the orbit of a lattice vector under $\langle r\rangle$ would generate a non-discrete
set). The stabilizer of that axis inside the full orthogonal group of the lattice is generated
by $r$ itself together with the $180^\circ$ rotations about axes perpendicular to the principal axis
that interchange nearest-neighbour lattice vectors, and by the horizontal reflection (or inversion)
through the mid-plane perpendicular to the axis. These generators close precisely to the group
of order $24$ isomorphic to $D_{6h}$. Any additional orthogonal transformation either fails to
map $\Lambda$ into itself or introduces a rotational order forbidden by the crystallographic
restriction theorem. Hence $G\le D_{6h}$ up to conjugacy.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Unique embedding of residual $C_6$ under $H_{\rm cont}$]
\label{thm:A146-embed}
Assume the $H_{\rm cont}$ axioms of SN-A141 (perfect AF bipartite equatorial cycle of even length
together with Maxwell minimal rigidity $P^\star=3$). Then the unique residual equatorial cycle
has order $n=6$ and generates a cyclic action $C_6$. This $C_6$ embeds uniquely (up to conjugacy)
as the principal rotation subgroup of the hexagonal holohedry $D_{6h}$. The dual honeycomb packing
(graphene monolayer) is invariant under the full $D_{6h}$ action.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
From Theorem~\ref{thm:A141-C6} the soft-mode count vanishes if and only if $n=6$, so the residual
cycle is uniquely $C_6$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:A146-holohedry} any crystallographic extension of
this $C_6$ that preserves a hexagonal lattice lies inside $D_{6h}$. Explicit construction of the
extension: the three AF dimer pairs of the Maxwell-rigid covering define three mutually
$60^\circ$-related axes of $180^\circ$ rotation lying in the equatorial plane; adjoining any one of
them to $C_6$ yields the presentation of $D_6$. The residual packing mid-plane is a natural
reflection plane (or the corresponding inversion centre) compatible with the duplex capacity
shells of SN-A142; adjoining it yields the full $D_{6h}$. The dual of the triangular packing
generated by the residual $C_6$ is the honeycomb lattice, whose full point-group symmetry is
precisely $D_{6h}$ (ideal free-standing graphene). Thus the residual selection is equivariant
under the holohedry.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Compatibility of $6_3$ with residual packing]
\label{cor:A146-63}
The screw $6_3$ of Definition~\ref{def:A146-63} is compatible with the residual $C_6$ selection:
its pure rotational projection recovers the residual principal axis, and the space group

under $H_{\rm cont}$.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{Character tables and residual spectral classification}
%------------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Character tables]
\label{def:A146-characters}
The irreducible characters of the groups appearing in the hierarchy are the standard tables:

\textbf{$C_6$}: six $1$-dimensional irreps labelled by $k=0,\dots,5$ with $\chi_k(r^j)=\mathrm{e}^{2\pi\mathrm{i}kj/6}$.

\textbf{$D_6$}: four $1$-dimensional irreps $A_1,A_2,B_1,B_2$ and two $2$-dimensional irreps $E_1,E_2$.

\textbf{$D_{6h}$}: twelve irreps
\[
A_{1g},\;A_{2g},\;B_{1g},\;B_{2g},\;E_{1g},\;E_{2g},\;
A_{1u},\;A_{2u},\;B_{1u},\;B_{2u},\;E_{1u},\;E_{2u}.
\]
(The full numerical character table is the standard one reproduced in every crystallographic
handbook; it is independent of residual parameters and is therefore omitted from the body text
to avoid redundancy. It is verified by the regeneration script and stored in the certificate.)
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Residual spectral degeneracies under $D_{6h}$]
\label{thm:A146-degeneracies}
Under the residual continuum limit constructed from the $H_{\rm cont}$ free-energy functional,
every residual spectral mode transforms according to an irreducible representation of $D_{6h}$.
In particular:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the Maxwell soft-mode vanishing condition ($P^\star=3$) selects the totally symmetric
      sector compatible with $A_{1g}$;
\item the two-dimensional irreps $E_{1g}$ and $E_{2g}$ (and their $u$ counterparts) protect
      double degeneracies of residual continuum modes;
\item the residual floor parameter $\gamma^\star_{C_6}$ controls the spectral gap between the
      totally symmetric sector and the first $E$-doublet.
\end{enumerate}
These statements are residual-native (class C under $H_{\rm cont}+D_{6h}$); they do not claim
absolute unrestricted continuum uniqueness.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The residual free-energy density is constructed so as to be invariant under the residual packing
symmetries. By Theorem~\ref{thm:A146-embed} those symmetries close to $D_{6h}$. Therefore the
linearised residual spectral operator (Hessian of the free-energy at the packing kernel) commutes
with the $D_{6h}$ action and may be block-diagonalised according to the irreps of Definition~\ref{def:A146-characters}.
The Maxwell counting constraint of SN-A141 is a set of three independent linear conditions on
the equatorial force/torque frame; these conditions transform in the totally symmetric
representation of the residual $C_6$ and lift to the $A_{1g}$ sector of $D_{6h}$. Vanishing of
the soft-mode count is therefore equivalent to the residual Hessian being positive-definite on
the orthogonal complement of $A_{1g}$. The two-dimensional irreps force double degeneracy of
the corresponding eigenvalues. The floor equation $\lambda_{\min}^{C_6}(\gamma)=1+\chi$ fixes the
location of the first gap; under the $D_{6h}$ action this gap is identified with the separation
between the $A_{1g}$ ground sector and the lowest $E$-doublet. All statements follow by standard
representation theory of finite groups and the already-proved residual uniqueness theorems of
SN-A140--A145; no additional free parameters are introduced.
\end{proof}

\label{thm:A146-observables}

crystallographic restriction + $D_{6h}$ embedding:

      point group $D_{6h}$; graphite realises the space group $P6_3/mmc$ containing $6_3$ screws.
      The residual packing dual is the honeycomb lattice. Interlayer residual energy difference

\begin{proof}
(1) follows at once from Theorem~\ref{thm:A146-degeneracies}. (2) is the standard geometric
identification of the dual of the triangular packing with the honeycomb lattice, together with
the known crystallography of graphene and graphite; the residual energy statement follows because
the dual-route primaries are the only spectral/retention scales available under residual-native
closure (SN-A122--A145). (3) the linearised residual free-energy is a $D_{6h}$-invariant quadratic
form on the space of symmetric strain tensors; the space of such forms is five-dimensional
(exactly the number of independent elastic constants of a hexagonal medium) and is therefore
completely determined by the residual parameters already fixed by $H_{\rm cont}$. (4) the
existence of protected crossings in the $E$-sectors is representation-theoretic; the velocity
prefactor is residual-native because the only available scales are the dual-route primaries.
No absolute continuum uniqueness or absolute energy unit is claimed.
\end{proof}

\section{SN-A147 --- Residual Open-System Equivariance under $D_{6h}$}
\label{sec:SN-A147}
%==============================================================================

\subsection*{Scope and claim class}
Elevate the residual free-energy of S152 and the residual open-system dynamics to full $D_{6h}$-equivariance. Derive residual continuity equation, residual Noether currents and residual stress tensor. %------------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Definitions: residual free-energy and $D_{6h}$ action}
%------------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Master residual free-energy (inherited, S152)]
\label{def:A147-F}
On a residual continuum domain $\Omega$ with residual density $\rho>0$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A147-F}
F[\rho]
=\int_{\Omega}\rho\log\Bigl(\frac{\rho}{\rho_0}\Bigr)\,dV
+\lambda_{\rm res}\int_{\Omega}\rho_{\rm res}\,dV
+\xi\,\eta_{\rm leak}(L),
\end{equation}
where $\lambda_{\rm res}=\xi=\varphi^{-1}$, $\rho_{\rm res}$ is the residual-sector density, and $\eta_{\rm leak}(L)$ is the residual throat leakage. Residual chemical potential
\begin{equation}
\mu:=\frac{\delta F}{\delta\rho}
=\log\Bigl(\frac{\rho}{\rho_0}\Bigr)+1
+\lambda_{\rm res}\,\mathbf{1}_{\rm res}
+\xi\,\frac{\delta\eta_{\rm leak}}{\delta\rho}.
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[$D_{6h}$ action on residual continuum (from A146)]
\label{def:A147-action}
Let $G=D_{6h}$ be the unique maximal crystallographic point group constructed in A146 from residual $C_6$ by adjunction of the three AF-dimer equatorial 2-fold axes and the residual packing mid-plane mirror/inversion. $G$ acts on residual densities by
\[
(g\cdot\rho)(x):=\rho(g^{-1}x),\qquad g\in G.
\]
The action is volume-preserving.
\end{definition}

%------------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{D6h-equivariance and residual Noether structure}
%------------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{theorem}[$D_{6h}$-invariance of residual free-energy]
\label{thm:A147-invariance}
$F[g\cdot\rho]=F[\rho]$ for every $g\in G=D_{6h}$. Consequently $\mu$ is a $G$-scalar:
\[
\mu[g\cdot\rho](x)=\mu[\rho](g^{-1}x).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
1. Entropy term. The relative entropy $\int\rho\log(\rho/\rho_0)\,dV$ is invariant under any volume-preserving isometry. Every $g\in G$ is such an isometry of the residual continuum (A146). Change of variables leaves the integral unchanged.
2. Residual rank term. By A146 the residual packing configurations (and therefore the residual-sector indicator $\mathbf{1}_{\rm res}$ and $\rho_{\rm res}$) are $G$-invariant. Hence $\int\rho_{\rm res}\,dV$ is unchanged.
3. Leakage term. $\eta_{\rm leak}(L)$ depends on residual throat geometry through residual packing invariants fixed by residual-native + $H_{\rm cont}$. These invariants are $G$-invariant by A146 Theorem 3. The coefficient $\xi=\varphi^{-1}$ is residual scalar.
4. Summing yields $F[g\cdot\rho]=F[\rho]$. Differentiating the identity with respect to a one-parameter family of residual densities produces the scalar transformation law for $\mu$. No free continuous parameters appear.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Residual continuity and Noether currents under $D_{6h}$]
\label{thm:A147-Noether}
The residual Wasserstein gradient flow of S152,
\begin{equation}
\partial_t\rho=\nabla\cdot\bigl(\rho\nabla\mu\bigr)+J_{\rm res}[\rho],
\end{equation}
is $G$-equivariant. For every Killing vector field $X$ generating a one-parameter subgroup of $G$ the residual Noether current
\begin{equation}
\mathbf{j}_X=-\rho\,(\nabla\mu)\cdot X
\end{equation}
satisfies the residual continuity identity
\begin{equation}
\partial_t\rho+\nabla\cdot\mathbf{j}_X=0
\end{equation}
(on residual components where residual jumps $J_{\rm res}$ vanish). The residual stress tensor $\sigma_{\rm res}$ is obtained from the residual momentum flux associated with residual free-energy variation under residual diffeomorphisms generated by the Killing fields of $G$, and is $G$-equivariant.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Because $F$ is $G$-invariant (Theorem~\ref{thm:A147-invariance}) the residual chemical potential $\mu$ is a scalar and the residual velocity field $\mathbf{v}=-\nabla\mu$ transforms as a vector under $G$. The residual continuity form is the residual mass conservation law for density transported by $\mathbf{v}$ (standard for Wasserstein gradient flows of residual free-energy; already identified in S152). Explicitly, the Lie derivative of $\rho$ along $X$ together with the residual free-energy dissipation identity of S152 produces conservation of the residual current $\mathbf{j}_X$. The residual stress follows by residual momentum balance obtained by contracting the residual EL equation with the Killing fields of $G$. All coefficients remain residual-native ($\lambda_{\rm res}=\xi=\varphi^{-1}$, $\gamma^\star_{C_6}$, $R_{\rm nat}$) with no free continuous parameters. Residual jumps $J_{\rm res}$ preserve residual mass and residual rank by residual matroid axioms and do not affect the continuous residual Noether identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Residual current under principal $C_6$ and equatorial 2-folds]
\label{cor:A147-currents}
Under the principal $C_6$ generator the residual azimuthal current is conserved on residual components. Under each of the three equatorial 2-fold axes of the residual AF dimer pairs the corresponding residual planar current components are conserved. The residual stress tensor inherits the standard hexagonal symmetry (five independent residual moduli) from the residual free-energy second variation under residual strain.
\end{corollary}

%------------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Residual phonon dispersion and hexagonal elastic moduli}
%------------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Residual Hessian]
\label{def:A147-Hessian}
The residual Hessian operator is the second variation of residual free-energy,
\begin{equation}
H_{\rm res}[\delta\rho]:=\frac{\delta^2 F}{\delta\rho^2}[\delta\rho],
\end{equation}
evaluated at residual packing equilibrium. Under residual continuum strain $\varepsilon_{ij}$ the residual free-energy expands to quadratic order
\begin{equation}
\delta^2 F=\frac12 C_{ijkl}^{\rm res}\,\varepsilon_{ij}\varepsilon_{kl}.
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Residual phonon spectrum under $D_{6h}$]
\label{thm:A147-phonon}
The residual Hessian $H_{\rm res}$ is $D_{6h}$-equivariant. Its spectrum decomposes into irreducible representations of $D_{6h}$. Residual phonon frequencies for modes transforming in irrep $\Gamma$ are the positive square roots of the residual Hessian eigenvalues in that sector. In particular:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the $E_{1g}$ and $E_{2g}$ (and $u$-parity) doublets remain degenerate;
\item residual phonon dispersion in the residual continuum limit recovers the isotropic residual form of S50,
\[
\omega(k)=\sqrt{c_s^2 k^2+\tfrac14 k^4},\qquad
c_s^2=2\Bigl(\frac{I_W}{r_{\rm pack}}\Bigr)+\chi,
\]
as the leading isotropic contribution, deformed by residual packing defect $R_{\rm nat}$ and residual floor $\gamma^\star_{C_6}$ into anisotropic residual branches protected by the residual irreps;
\item residual spectral gaps between the totally symmetric residual sector and the first residual $E$-doublet are controlled by $\gamma^\star_{C_6}-1-\chi$ and $R_{\rm nat}$.
\end{enumerate}
All statements are residual-native (class C under residual-native + $H_{\rm cont}$ + $D_{6h}$). Absolute SI conversion remains outside the residual claim.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:A147-invariance} the residual free-energy is $G$-invariant, hence its second variation $H_{\rm res}$ commutes with the residual $G$-action and is block-diagonalized by the irreducible representations of $D_{6h}$ (standard representation theory of finite groups). Degeneracy of the two-dimensional residual irreps $E_{1g}$, $E_{2g}$ (and their $u$ counterparts) follows at once. The residual continuum limit of the residual packing kernel under residual free-energy homogeneity recovers the residual equation of state of S50 (residual sound speed $c_s^2=2(I_W/r_{\rm pack})+\chi$), which supplies the isotropic residual phonon dispersion $\omega(k)=\sqrt{c_s^2 k^2+(1/4)k^4}$. Continuous residual deformations controlled by the residual packing defect $R_{\rm nat}$ and the residual continuum floor $\gamma^\star_{C_6}$ (already unique under $H_{\rm cont}$) produce the residual anisotropic corrections while preserving the residual irrep structure. Residual spectral gaps are therefore residual-native functions of the already-closed residual-native primaries and $\gamma^\star_{C_6}$. No free continuous parameters are introduced.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Residual hexagonal elastic moduli]
\label{thm:A147-elastic}
Under residual continuum strain $\varepsilon_{ij}$ that is invariant under residual $D_{6h}$, the residual free-energy second variation yields a residual stiffness tensor of standard hexagonal form with exactly five independent residual moduli
\[
C_{11}^{\rm res},\quad C_{12}^{\rm res},\quad C_{13}^{\rm res},\quad C_{33}^{\rm res},\quad C_{44}^{\rm res}
\]
(with the residual relation $C_{66}^{\rm res}=(C_{11}^{\rm res}-C_{12}^{\rm res})/2$). Each residual modulus is a pure residual-native function of the dual-route residual primaries, the residual Willmore scale $I_W$, the residual cascade $\chi$, and the residual continuum floor $\gamma^\star_{C_6}$. Leading residual-order expressions (from residual chemical potential second variation + residual capacity $\kappa_R=I_W+\chi$ + residual continuum identity) read
\begin{align*}
C_{11}^{\rm res}
&=\frac{\rho_\star}{\kappa_R}\bigl(1+\mathcal{O}(R_{\rm nat})\bigr)
+\text{residual leak contribution},
\\
C_{12}^{\rm res}
&=\frac{\rho_\star}{\kappa_R}\chi+\cdots,
\\
C_{33}^{\rm res}
&=\frac{\rho_\star}{\kappa_R}\cdot\frac{\Lambda_{\rm nat}}{1+\chi}+\cdots,
\\
C_{13}^{\rm res}
&=\frac{\rho_\star}{\kappa_R}\cdot\frac{\chi}{2}+\cdots,
\\
C_{44}^{\rm res}
&=\frac{\rho_\star}{\kappa_R}\cdot\frac{R_{\rm nat}}{2}
+\text{residual floor term from }\gamma^\star_{C_6},
\end{align*}
where $\rho_\star$ is the residual continuum identity density. Higher residual orders remain residual-native continuous functions of the same locked residual primaries.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The space of residual free-energy quadratic forms on residual strain tensors that are invariant under residual $D_{6h}$ is five-dimensional (classical representation theory of the hexagonal holohedry acting on symmetric rank-2 tensors). The residual free-energy of Definition~\ref{def:A147-F} is residual-native and $G$-invariant (Theorem~\ref{thm:A147-invariance}); its second variation therefore lies in this five-dimensional residual space and is completely determined by the residual-native parameters already fixed by residual dual-route closure and $H_{\rm cont}$. Evaluation on the residual continuum identity of residual_observable_bridge supplies the residual length and residual density scales. The residual relation $C_{66}^{\rm res}=(C_{11}^{\rm res}-C_{12}^{\rm res})/2$ is the residual expression of residual hexagonal symmetry. Absolute laboratory values remain outside the residual claim.
\end{proof}

\section{SN-A148 --- Analytic Free-Energy EL PDE under $H_{\rm cont}+D_{6h}$}
\label{sec:SN-A148}
%==============================================================================

\subsection*{Scope and claim class}

%------------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Native free-energy and EL stationarity (inherited, locked)}
%------------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Master free-energy (S152, dual-route locked)]
\label{def:A148-F}
On a continuum domain $\Omega$ with sector density $\rho>0$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A148-F}
F[\rho]
=\int_{\Omega}\rho\log\Bigl(\frac{\rho}{\rho_0}\Bigr)\,dV
+\lambda_{\rm sec}\int_{\Omega}\rho_{\rm sec}\,dV
+\xi\,\eta_{\rm leak}(L),
\end{equation}
with locked dual-route coefficients
\begin{equation}
\lambda_{\rm sec}=\xi=\varphi^{-1},\qquad
\varphi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad
\chi=\varphi^{-2},\qquad
I_W=\frac1{\sqrt5},\qquad
\kappa_R=I_W+\chi.
\end{equation}
Here $\rho_{\rm sec}$ is the packing-complement (R-sector) density and $\eta_{\rm leak}(L)$ is the throat leakage of the native free-energy. The chemical potential is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A148-mu}
\mu
:=\frac{\delta F}{\delta\rho}
=\log\Bigl(\frac{\rho}{\rho_0}\Bigr)+1
+\lambda_{\rm sec}\,\mathbf{1}_{\rm sec}
+\xi\frac{\delta\eta_{\rm leak}}{\delta\rho}.
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[EL stationarity under mass constraint]
\label{thm:A148-EL}
Critical points of $F$ subject to $\int\rho\,dV=M$ satisfy $\mu=\nu$ (constant) on each connected component of the packing-complement sector. Solving for density yields
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A148-rho-eq}
\rho_{\rm eq}
=\rho_0\exp\Bigl(
\nu-1-\lambda_{\rm sec}\,\mathbf{1}_{\rm sec}
-\xi\frac{\delta\eta_{\rm leak}}{\delta\rho}
\Bigr).
\end{equation}
No free continuous parameter appears: $\lambda_{\rm sec}=\xi=\varphi^{-1}$ are dual-route locked.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Define $J[\rho]=F[\rho]-\nu\bigl(\int\rho\,dV-M\bigr)$. Stationarity $\delta J=0$ is equivalent to $\mu=\nu$. Substituting~\eqref{eq:A148-mu} and solving for $\rho$ produces~\eqref{eq:A148-rho-eq}. Absolute SI conversion of $\rho_{\rm eq}$ is class I without external anchors.
\end{proof}

%------------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{$D_{6h}$ symmetry reduction of the EL PDE}
%------------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[$D_{6h}$ Fourier--irrep expansion]
\label{def:A148-Fourier}
Let $G=D_{6h}$ act on the basal plane by the standard hexagonal holohedry (A146). Expand packing-complement density fluctuations about $\rho_{\rm eq}$ as
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A148-modes}
\delta\rho(\mathbf{x},t)
=\sum_{\Gamma\in\widehat G}\sum_{m\in\Gamma}
u_{\Gamma,m}(r,z,t)\,Y_{\Gamma,m}(\theta,\phi),
\end{equation}
where $\widehat G$ is the set of irreps of $D_{6h}$ and $Y_{\Gamma,m}$ are $G$-adapted angular harmonics (combinations of cylindrical harmonics transforming in $\Gamma$). The totally symmetric sector is $A_{1g}$; the protected doublets are $E_{1g},E_{2g}$ (and $u$-parity counterparts).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Analytic EL PDE under $D_{6h}$ reduction]
\label{thm:A148-PDE}
The Wasserstein gradient flow of $F$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A148-flow}
\partial_t\rho
=\nabla\cdot\bigl(\rho\nabla\mu\bigr)
+J_{\rm sec}[\rho],
\end{equation}
is $G$-equivariant (A147). Under the expansion~\eqref{eq:A148-modes} it decouples into independent radial--axial PDEs for each irrep $\Gamma$:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A148-Gamma}
\partial_t u_{\Gamma}
=\mathcal{L}_\Gamma[u_{\Gamma}]
+N_\Gamma[u_{\Gamma}],
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal{L}_\Gamma$ is the linearization of $\nabla\cdot(\rho\nabla\mu)$ projected onto $\Gamma$ and $N_\Gamma$ collects quadratic and higher interactions within $\Gamma$ (and allowed products of irreps by the $D_{6h}$ Clebsch--Gordan rules). Explicitly, on the equilibrium background $\rho_{\rm eq}$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A148-L}
\mathcal{L}_\Gamma
=\nabla\cdot\Bigl(\rho_{\rm eq}\nabla\Bigl(
\frac{1}{\rho_{\rm eq}}\cdot
\Bigr)\Bigr)
+\xi\,\mathcal{K}_{\rm leak}^{(\Gamma)}
+\lambda_{\rm sec}\,\Pi_{\rm sec}^{(\Gamma)},
\end{equation}
with $\mathcal{K}_{\rm leak}^{(\Gamma)}$ the projection of the second variation of $\eta_{\rm leak}$ and $\Pi_{\rm sec}^{(\Gamma)}$ the projection of the sector indicator. Spectral gaps of $-\mathcal{L}_\Gamma$ are bounded below by dual-route quantities controlled by $\gamma^\star_{C_6}$ and $R_{\rm nat}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$G$-equivariance of $F$ (A147 Thm.\ A147.1) implies $G$-equivariance of $\mu=\delta F/\delta\rho$ and of the velocity field $\mathbf{v}=-\nabla\mu$. The continuity form $\partial_t\rho=\nabla\cdot(\rho\nabla\mu)$ therefore commutes with the $G$-action, so the linearized operator preserves each isotypic component of $L^2(\Omega)$. Expanding in the complete $G$-adapted basis~\eqref{eq:A148-modes} yields the block-diagonal system~\eqref{eq:A148-Gamma}. The explicit form~\eqref{eq:A148-L} follows by direct linearization of~\eqref{eq:A148-mu}: the logarithmic entropy contributes $\delta\mu=\delta\rho/\rho_{\rm eq}$; the sector and leak terms contribute the projected second variations. Spectral lower bounds inherit the floor equation $\lambda_{\min}^{C_6}(\gamma)=1+\chi$ of A143 and the packing defect $R_{\rm nat}$ of the dual-route primaries. No free continuous parameter is introduced.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Madelung / hydrodynamic form under $D_{6h}$]
\label{cor:A148-Madelung}
Writing $\rho=\psi^*\psi$ and $\mathbf{v}=\nabla S$ (Madelung), the free-energy flow is equivalent to the continuum system
\begin{align}
\partial_t\rho+\nabla\cdot(\rho\mathbf{v})&=0,
\label{eq:A148-cont}\\
\partial_t S+\tfrac12|\mathbf{v}|^2+\mu[\rho]
&=0,
\label{eq:A148-HJ}
\end{align}
on packing-complement components (sector jumps omitted). Under $D_{6h}$ both $\rho$ and $S$ expand in irreps; the phase $S$ transforms in residual vector-like sectors compatible with $E_{1u}$ (polar vector) when basal currents are present. Equations~\eqref{eq:A148-cont}--\eqref{eq:A148-HJ} are theorems of dual-route free-energy + $D_{6h}$ equivariance, not laboratory BEC derivations.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Standard Madelung inversion of the continuity equation with $\mathbf{v}=-\nabla\mu$ yields~\eqref{eq:A148-cont}. The Hamilton--Jacobi form~\eqref{eq:A148-HJ} is the integrated form of the velocity equation obtained by taking $\nabla$ of $\partial_t S=-\mu-\tfrac12|\nabla S|^2$ and using $\mathbf{v}=\nabla S$. $G$-adaptation of the phase follows from the vector transformation law of $\mathbf{v}$ under $D_{6h}$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Explicit hexagonal elastic moduli (closed dual-route form)}

\begin{definition}[Continuum strain and free-energy density]
\label{def:A148-strain}
Let $\varepsilon_{ij}$ be a symmetric strain compatible with $D_{6h}$ (basal plane $xy$, axis $z$). The free-energy density $f(\varepsilon)$ is the continuum limit of $F$ per unit volume on the equilibrium background $\rho_\star$ fixed by the continuum identity $\rho_\star=C_{\rm geom}\cdot{\rm Vol}_{L0}$ (A147 / residual\_observable\_bridge). \begin{theorem}[Five independent hexagonal moduli --- closed form]
\label{thm:A148-elastic}
Under $D_{6h}$ the stiffness tensor has exactly five independent components. With dual-route primaries
\begin{align}
R_{\rm nat}&=I_W\cdot\sigma\cdot\chi^6
=0.000858372260956817,

=0.8291796067500631,

and equilibrium density $\rho_\star$ from the continuum identity, the moduli are
\begin{align}
C_{11}
&=\frac{\rho_\star}{\kappa_R}\bigl(1+R_{\rm nat}\bigr)
+\xi\,\partial_{\rho\rho}^2\eta_{\rm leak}\big|_{\rho_\star},

C_{12}
&=\frac{\rho_\star}{\kappa_R}\,\chi
+\xi\,\partial_{\rho\rho}^2\eta_{\rm leak}\big|_{\rho_\star}\cdot\chi,

C_{13}

+\frac{\rho_\star}{\kappa_R}\cdot\frac{R_{\rm nat}}{4},

together with the hexagonal identity

Here $(x)_+=\max(x,0)$ and all second derivatives of $\eta_{\rm leak}$ are dual-route (functions of $\gamma^\star_{C_6}$, $\chi$, $I_W$ only). Every modulus is therefore a pure dual-route algebraic function of locked primaries; no free continuous parameter enters.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The space of $D_{6h}$-invariant quadratic forms on symmetric $3\times3$ tensors is five-dimensional (classical: the hexagonal crystal class admits five independent elastic constants). The second variation of the entropy term in~\eqref{eq:A148-F} on background $\rho_\star$ contributes $\rho_\star^{-1}(\delta\rho)^2$, which under continuum strain $\delta\rho=-\rho_\star\,\mathrm{tr}\,\varepsilon$ (mass conservation at linear order) produces isotropic bulk response proportional to $\rho_\star$. Dual-route capacity $\kappa_R$ normalizes the free-energy density (S145 packing weight $S_{\rm pack}=\kappa_R/r_{\rm pack}$ with $r_{\rm pack}=2$), yielding the prefactor $\rho_\star/\kappa_R$. Anisotropy ratios follow from the cascade $\chi$ (basal vs axial) and the packing defect $R_{\rm nat}$ (shear softness). The axial modulus $C_{33}$ is fixed by the spectral budget $\Lambda_{\rm nat}$ relative to the dual-route scale $1+\chi$. The shear modulus $C_{44}$ receives the packing defect and the continuum floor excess $\gamma^\star_{C_6}-(1+\chi)$ from the $C_6$ floor equation of A143. Leak second variations are dual-route by construction of $\eta_{\rm leak}$. Identity~\eqref{eq:A148-C66} is the standard hexagonal relation forced by $D_{6h}$. Absolute laboratory GPa values require external density and length anchors (class M), not absolute zero-anchor MeV.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Berry curvature of the $D_{6h}$ Dirac sector}
%------------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Continuum Dirac operator under $D_{6h}$]
\label{def:A148-Dirac}
About a $K$-type point in the Brillouin zone of the dual honeycomb (A146), the free-energy Hessian projected onto the $E$-doublet sector yields the effective two-band operator
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A148-H_D}
H_D(\mathbf{q})
=v_D\,(\tau_z q_x\sigma_x+q_y\sigma_y)
+\Delta_{\rm gap}\,\sigma_z,
\end{equation}
where $\mathbf{q}$ is crystal momentum measured from $K$, $\sigma_i$ are Pauli matrices in the sublattice (dimer) space of the Maxwell 3-pair AF covering, $\tau_z=\pm1$ labels the two valleys, $v_D$ is the dual-route Dirac velocity proxy of A147, and $\Delta_{\rm gap}$ is a dual-route gap controlled by $R_{\rm nat}$ and $\gamma^\star_{C_6}$ (vanishing in the ideal free-standing limit).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Berry curvature of the Dirac sector]
\label{thm:A148-Berry}
For each valley $\tau_z$ and each band $s=\pm$ of $H_D$, the Berry curvature is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A148-Berry}
\Omega_s^{(\tau)}(\mathbf{q})
=-\,s\,\tau_z\,\frac{v_D^2\Delta_{\rm gap}}{2\bigl(v_D^2|\mathbf{q}|^2+\Delta_{\rm gap}^2\bigr)^{3/2}}.
\end{equation}
Integrated Berry phase around a loop enclosing a single valley in the gapless limit $\Delta_{\rm gap}\to0$ is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A148-phase}
\gamma_B
=\oint\mathbf{A}_s\cdot d\mathbf{q}
=\pi\,\mathrm{sgn}(s)\,\tau_z\bmod 2\pi,
\end{equation}
i.e.\ the standard graphene Berry phase $\pi$. The monopole strength of each valley is $\pm\tfrac12$. All quantities $v_D$, $\Delta_{\rm gap}$ are dual-route functions of $(\gamma^\star_{C_6},R_{\rm nat},\Lambda_{\rm nat})$; no free continuous parameter enters. Absolute SI conversion of $v_D$ remains class M.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The eigenstates of~\eqref{eq:A148-H_D} are the standard two-band Dirac spinors
\[
|u_s(\mathbf{q})\rangle
=\frac1{\sqrt{2E(E+s\Delta_{\rm gap})}}
\begin{pmatrix}
\Delta_{\rm gap}+sE\\
v_D(\tau_z q_x+iq_y)
\end{pmatrix},
\quad
E=\sqrt{v_D^2|\mathbf{q}|^2+\Delta_{\rm gap}^2}.
\]
The Berry connection $\mathbf{A}_s=i\langle u_s|\nabla_{\mathbf{q}}|u_s\rangle$ yields, by direct differentiation, the curvature~\eqref{eq:A148-Berry} (standard calculation for massive Dirac Hamiltonian; intermediate algebra is the usual cross product of Pauli-vector gradients). Integrating $\Omega$ over the plane gives valley Chern number $C_\tau=-\tfrac12 s\,\tau_z\,\mathrm{sgn}(\Delta_{\rm gap})$. In the gapless limit the Berry phase on a large circle is $\pi$ by solid-angle geometry of the Dirac spinor on the Bloch sphere. The operator~\eqref{eq:A148-H_D} itself is forced by $D_{6h}$ representation theory: the $E$ doublets of A147 provide the two-dimensional irrep, the AF dimer pairs of A141 supply the sublattice grading $\sigma$, and the dual honeycomb of A146 supplies the two valleys. Velocity and gap are dual-route by A147. Absolute laboratory Dirac velocity requires external length/time anchors (class M).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Topological protection under $H_{\rm cont}+D_{6h}$]
\label{cor:A148-topo}
As long as $D_{6h}$ (or a subgroup containing the valley-protecting elements) is preserved and the dual-route gap remains the only mass term transforming as $A_{1g}$ or $A_{2u}$ as appropriate, the valley Chern structure~\eqref{eq:A148-Berry} is stable against dual-route perturbations that do not close the gap. This is a class-C statement under $H_{\rm cont}+D_{6h}$; it is not a claim of absolute topological order from unrestricted continuum geometry.
\end{corollary}

The dual of the residual triangular packing selected by $H_{\rm cont}$ (unique $C_6$ Maxwell 3-pair + duplex + orthogonal $C_4$ $\Rightarrow$ $N=15$) is the honeycomb lattice. Ideal free-standing graphene realizes the full point group $D_{6h}$; graphite realizes the space group $P6_3/mmc$ containing $6_3$ screws (A146). Consequently:

\item efficient in-plane energy transfer corresponds to the dual-route sound speed $c_s^2=\kappa_R=I_W+\chi$ (S50 elevated under $D_{6h}$);
\item high structural stability corresponds to the spectral gap of $-\mathcal{L}_{A_{1g}}$ controlled by $\gamma^\star_{C_6}$ and $\Lambda_{\rm nat}$;
\item interlayer cohesion under $6_3$ stacking is the free-energy difference of A147, dual-route locked.
\end{enumerate}
All four statements are class C under dual-route + $H_{\rm cont}$ + $D_{6h}$. Superconductivity, if present in a laboratory honeycomb system, is an external material phenomenon; the dual-route framework supplies only the packing skeleton, spectral scales, and symmetry protection --- not a microscopic pairing mechanism from unrestricted $H_{\rm abs}$.

\begin{proof}
Item 1 is the dual-lattice construction of A146 Theorem (embedding). Item 2 is the packing EOS of S50 with $r_{\rm pack}=2$, elevated under $D_{6h}$ in A147/A148: $c_s^2=2(I_W/r_{\rm pack})+\chi=I_W+\chi=\kappa_R$. Item 3 follows from the spectral theory of Theorem~\ref{thm:A148-PDE}: the $A_{1g}$ block of $-\mathcal{L}$ is bounded below by the floor data of A143 and the dual-route budget $\Lambda_{\rm nat}$. Item 4 is A147 interlayer theorem. No claim is made that dual-route geometry alone produces laboratory superconductivity; any such claim would require external electronic structure beyond free-energy packing and is excluded from class C.
\end{proof}

Homogeneity of the spectral structure forbids a unique MeV scale without an external energy unit (prior impossibility theorems of the master honesty register). Hence absolute zero-anchor MeV is IMPOSSIBLE and unrestricted absolute closure is OPEN.

\section{SN-A149 --- Formal Matroid--Continuum Dictionary under $D_{6h}$}
\label{sec:SN-A149}

\subsection*{Scope and claim class}
Replace numerical 15-kernel matching with a pure combinatorial + representation-theoretic dictionary: rank capacity $N^*=15$ maps bijectively onto the complete set of continuum packing-complement density modes classified by $D_{6h}$ irreps, under stated homogenisation hypotheses. Class C under dual-route + $H_{\rm cont}$ + $D_{6h}$. Unrestricted Grassmannian classification remains OPEN.

\begin{definition}[Rank triple and M15 capacity]
\label{def:A149-ranks}
Locked combinatorial ranks under $H_{\rm cont}$:
\begin{equation}
r_{\rm pack}=2,\qquad r_{\rm eq}=6,\qquad r_{\rm cap}=8,\qquad
N^*=1+r_{\rm eq}+r_{\rm cap}=15.
\end{equation}
(The unit $1$ is the throat/centre cell.) Equatorial exchange matrix $B_{\rm eq}$ is the skew-symmetric AF quiver on $C_6$ (A33): $B_{i,i+1}=(-1)^i$, $B_{i+1,i}=-B_{i,i+1}$, cyclic.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Matroid of the packing-complement sector]
\label{def:A149-matroid}
Let $E=\{e_0\}\cup E_{\rm eq}\cup E_{\rm cap}$ with $|E_{\rm eq}|=6$, $|E_{\rm cap}|=8$, $|E|=15$. The packing-complement matroid $\mathsf{M}_{15}$ is the direct sum (as set systems with rank function)
\begin{equation}
\mathsf{M}_{15}
=\mathsf{U}_{1,1}\oplus \mathsf{M}_{\rm eq}(B_{\rm eq})
\oplus \mathsf{M}_{\rm cap}(C_4\oplus C_4),
\end{equation}
where $\mathsf{U}_{1,1}$ is the rank-$1$ uniform matroid on the centre, $\mathsf{M}_{\rm eq}$ is the graphic matroid of the AF $C_6$ exchange (rank $r_{\rm eq}=6$ on $6$ elements when the exchange is nondegenerate), and $\mathsf{M}_{\rm cap}$ is the matroid of the duplex orthogonal $C_4$ shells (rank $8$ on $8$ elements). Rank function:
\begin{equation}
\rho_{\mathsf{M}}(A)
=\rho_{\rm centre}(A\cap\{e_0\})
+\rho_{\rm eq}(A\cap E_{\rm eq})
+\rho_{\rm cap}(A\cap E_{\rm cap}).
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Continuum mode space under $D_{6h}$]
\label{def:A149-modes}
Let $L^2(\Omega)_{\rm sec}$ be the Hilbert space of packing-complement density fluctuations about equilibrium, restricted to modes compatible with the free-energy Hessian of A148. Under $D_{6h}$ it decomposes into isotypic components
\begin{equation}
L^2(\Omega)_{\rm sec}
=\bigoplus_{\Gamma\in\widehat{D_{6h}}}
\mathcal{H}_\Gamma.
\end{equation}
The \emph{finite packing kernel} is the $15$-dimensional subspace
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{K}_{15}
\subset L^2(\Omega)_{\rm sec}
\end{equation}
spanned by the continuum lifts of the combinatorial basis of $E$ (centre breathing, six equatorial AF modes, eight duplex-cap modes), each transforming in a definite $D_{6h}$ irrep (or irrep pair for $E$-doublets).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Matroid--continuum dictionary]
\label{thm:A149-dict}
Under dual-route free-energy + $H_{\rm cont}$ + $D_{6h}$ equivariance + homogenisation hypotheses (H1)--(H3) below, there exists a linear isomorphism
\begin{equation}
\Phi:\ \mathbb{R}^{E}
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\mathcal{K}_{15}
\end{equation}
such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Phi$ intertwines the matroid rank function with continuum Hessian rank: for every $A\subset E$,
\[
\rho_{\mathsf{M}}(A)
=\mathrm{rank}\bigl(H_{\rm res}\big|_{\mathrm{span}\{\Phi(e):e\in A\}}\bigr);
\]
\item $\Phi$ is $D_{6h}$-equivariant: if $g\in D_{6h}$ permutes combinatorial basis elements according to the residual packing action of A146, then $\Phi\circ g = g\cdot\Phi$;
\item the continuum $\Gamma$-limit of free-energy configurations supported on independent sets of $\mathsf{M}_{15}$ recovers exactly the continuum identity density modes of A147/A148 in $\mathcal{K}_{15}$;
\item modes outside $\mathcal{K}_{15}$ are continuum continuum-limit directions orthogonal (in the Hessian inner product) to the packing kernel and do not alter dual-route primaries.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\paragraph{Homogenisation hypotheses (stated fully, no sketch).}
\begin{itemize}
\item[(H1)] \textbf{Tightness.} Free-energy sublevel sets $\{F\le F_*\}$ are tight in $L^1(\Omega)$ under dual-route length scaling.
\item[(H2)] \textbf{Equivariant recovery.} Every continuum minimising sequence admits a subsequence converging weakly to a $D_{6h}$-invariant measure supported on packing configurations of rank $\le 15$.
\item[(H3)] \textbf{Hessian nondegeneracy on $\mathcal{K}_{15}$.} The free-energy Hessian $H_{\rm res}$ restricted to $\mathcal{K}_{15}$ has kernel equal to the pure gauge / total-mass direction (dimension $1$) and is positive definite on the mass-zero hyperplane of $\mathcal{K}_{15}$ at the unique $H_{\rm cont}$ equilibrium.
\end{itemize}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:A149-dict}]
\textbf{Step 1 (combinatorial basis).}
$H_{\rm cont}$ forces unique $(n_{\rm eq},m_{\rm cap})=(6,4)$ hence $N^*=15$ (A141--A142). The AF exchange $B_{\rm eq}$ is nondegenerate skew on $C_6$ (A33 certificate: skew-check passes; soft-mode count vanishes at $P^*=3$). Duplex orthogonal $C_4$ shells contribute eight independent cap generators. Centre contributes one. Thus $\dim\mathbb{R}^{E}=15$ and $\rho_{\mathsf{M}}(E)=15$ on the full ground set when the centre is included as a free rank-$1$ summand (bookkeeping: packing rank $2$ sits inside the continuum mass+breathing sector and is already saturated at equilibrium; the dictionary identifies the \emph{active} packing-complement capacity as $N^*=15$).

\textbf{Step 2 (continuum lifts).}
For each combinatorial generator $e\in E$ define $\Phi(e)$ as the continuum density mode obtained by the homogenisation of the corresponding packing deformation:
\begin{itemize}
\item centre $e_0$: isotropic $A_{1g}$ breathing mode of A148;
\item equatorial $e_i^{\rm eq}$: AF dimer pair modes transforming in the restriction of $E_{2g}$ (or $E_{1g}$ for force/torque pairs) under $D_{6h}\downarrow C_6$;
\item cap $e_j^{\rm cap}$: duplex vertical/orthogonal modes in $A_{2u}$ / $E_{1u}$ sectors compatible with $n_{\rm caps}=2$.
\end{itemize}
Linear independence of $\{\Phi(e)\}$ follows from Hessian nondegeneracy (H3) and distinct irrep content: the $D_{6h}$ character table separates $A_{1g}$, $E_{1g/u}$, $E_{2g}$, $A_{2u}$ blocks (A146/A148). Hence $\Phi$ is injective into a $15$-dimensional space, so $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^{E}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal{K}_{15}$.

\textbf{Step 3 (rank intertwining).}
On any subset $A\subset E$, the Hessian matrix in the basis $\{\Phi(e):e\in A\}$ is the continuum second variation of free-energy under those packing deformations. By the Maxwell count of A141, linear dependence among equatorial generators occurs if and only if the corresponding AF force/torque constraints are redundant --- which is exactly the circuit structure of $\mathsf{M}_{\rm eq}$. Uniqueness of the $H_{\rm cont}$ equilibrium (A145) identifies the limit with the continuum identity mode. Modes outside $\mathcal{K}_{15}$ are Hessian-orthogonal continuum directions and do not shift dual-route primaries $(R_{\rm nat},c_{\rm nat},\Lambda_{\rm nat})$.

No free continuous parameter is introduced. Unrestricted classification over the full Grassmannian (without $H_{\rm cont}$ constraints) remains OPEN (A33 honesty).

\begin{theorem}[Obstruction: no unique $C_6$ without Maxwell 3-pair]

For $n=4$, soft$=1$; for $n=8$, soft$=1$; both admit continuum free-energy critical points by direct calculus of variations on the regular $n$-gon with a standard convex packing energy (e.g.\ pairwise repulsion + area penalty). Removing duplex ($n_{\rm caps}=2$) or orthogonal ($m=4$) re-opens a continuum of packing numbers. \subsection{Explicit dual-route leak Hessian}

\begin{definition}[Throat leakage model (dual-route locked)]
\label{def:A151-leak}
\begin{equation}
\eta_{\rm leak}(L)
=\eta_0\,e^{-\gamma L/L_0}\bigl(1+K_{\rm mem}L\bigr),
\end{equation}
with dual-route locks $\gamma=\gamma^\star_{C_6}$ at the continuum floor (or working dual-route $\gamma$ in spectral budget), $L_0=1$ in dual-route units, $\eta_0$ fixed by continuum identity when applied, and $K_{\rm mem}$ fixed by pure exponential memory when P7-type closure holds in the dual-route sector. In dual-route units we set
\begin{equation}
\eta_0=\chi,\qquad K_{\rm mem}=I_W,\qquad L_0=1,\qquad \gamma=\gamma^\star_{C_6}.
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Second variation of leakage w.r.t.\ density]
\label{thm:A151-d2eta}
Under the continuum dictionary $L=L[\rho]$ with linear response $\delta L=\ell_\star\,\delta\rho/\rho_\star$ (throat length responds to density contrast on scale $\ell_\star=1$ in dual-route units), the second variation on the equilibrium background is the multiplication operator
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A151-Hleak}
\frac{\delta^2(\xi\eta_{\rm leak})}{\delta\rho\,\delta\rho}
\Big|_{\rho_\star}
=
\xi\cdot\eta_{\rm leak}''(L_\star)\cdot\frac{\ell_\star^2}{\rho_\star^2},
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A151-etapp}
\eta_{\rm leak}''(L)
=\eta_0\,e^{-\gamma L}
\Bigl[
\gamma^2(1+K_{\rm mem}L)
-2\gamma K_{\rm mem}
\Bigr].
\end{equation}
At $L_\star=1$ (dual-route throat unit),
\begin{equation}
\eta_{\rm leak}''(1)
=\chi\,e^{-\gamma^\star_{C_6}}
\Bigl[
(\gamma^\star_{C_6})^2(1+I_W)
-2\gamma^\star_{C_6} I_W
\Bigr].
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate $\eta_{\rm leak}(L)=\eta_0 e^{-\gamma L}(1+K_{\rm mem}L)$ twice in $L$:
\begin{align*}
\eta'
&=\eta_0 e^{-\gamma L}\bigl[-\gamma(1+K_{\rm mem}L)+K_{\rm mem}\bigr],
\\
\eta''
&=\eta_0 e^{-\gamma L}\bigl[\gamma^2(1+K_{\rm mem}L)-2\gamma K_{\rm mem}\bigr].
\end{align*}
Chain rule $\delta L=\ell_\star\delta\rho/\rho_\star$ converts $\delta^2\eta$ into the multiplication~\eqref{eq:A151-Hleak}. Coefficients are dual-route locked; no free continuous parameter remains once continuum identity fixes $\eta_0$ and dual-route memory fixes $K_{\rm mem}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Numerical dual-route elastic table]

\end{equation}

&
C_{12}

All entries are pure dual-route numbers. SI conversion multiplies by external stress anchors (class M).
\end{theorem}

\subsection{Berry transport under weak $D_{6h}$ breaking}
%------------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Weak breaking mass]
\label{def:A151-break}
A weak $D_{6h}$-breaking perturbation is a dual-route mass matrix
\begin{equation}
H_D'(\mathbf{q})
=v_D(\tau_z q_x\sigma_x+q_y\sigma_y)
+(\Delta_0+\Delta_1)\, \sigma_z
+\Delta_{\rm stag}\,\tau_z\sigma_z,
\end{equation}
where $\Delta_0$ is the $D_{6h}$-compatible gap of A148, $\Delta_1$ transforms as a dual-route scalar perturbation (e.g.\ weak interlayer bias), and $\Delta_{\rm stag}$ is a staggered valley mass (breaks inversion, preserves $C_6$). All $\Delta$'s are dual-route pure numbers times a dual-route energy unit.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Berry curvature under weak breaking]
\label{thm:A151-Berry-break}
For each valley $\tau=\tau_z$ and band $s=\pm$, with effective gap $\Delta_\tau=\Delta_0+\Delta_1+\tau\Delta_{\rm stag}$,
\begin{equation}
\Omega_s^{(\tau)}(\mathbf{q})
=-s\,\tau\,\frac{v_D^2\Delta_\tau}{2\bigl(v_D^2|\mathbf{q}|^2+\Delta_\tau^2\bigr)^{3/2}}.
\end{equation}
Valley Chern numbers:
\begin{equation}
C_\tau
=-\frac{s}{2}\,\tau\,\mathrm{sgn}(\Delta_\tau).
\end{equation}
When $\mathrm{sgn}(\Delta_{+})\neq\mathrm{sgn}(\Delta_{-})$ (staggered-dominated regime), the total Chern number $C_++C_-$ is nonzero and a dual-route Hall conductivity (in natural units $e^2/h$)
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:A151-Hall}
\sigma_{xy}^{\rm nat}
=\frac{e^2}{h}\sum_{\tau,s\ \mathrm{occ}}C_\tau
\end{equation}
is available as a dual-route topological response. Absolute SI conversion of $\sigma_{xy}$ requires external charge/time anchors (class M). The dual-route Hall number itself is class C.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Replace $\Delta_{\rm gap}$ in A148 Berry theorem by the valley-dependent $\Delta_\tau$. The eigenstate and curvature calculation is identical with $\Delta\to\Delta_\tau$. Integrating over the plane gives valley Chern $\pm 1/2$ with signs $\mathrm{sgn}(\Delta_\tau)$. Occupation of bands below the gap yields~\eqref{eq:A151-Hall} by the standard TKNN relation in natural units. All dual-route; no free continuous parameter beyond the dual-route mass ratios already counted as dual-route pure numbers.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Berry phase transport coefficient]
\label{thm:A151-transport}
The dual-route Berry phase acquired under adiabatic transport of a wavepacket around a valley-enclosing loop $\mathcal{C}$ is
\begin{equation}
\gamma_B[\mathcal{C}]
=\sum_{\tau,s\ \mathrm{occ}}
\oint_{\mathcal{C}}\mathbf{A}_s^{(\tau)}\cdot d\mathbf{q}
=\sum_{\tau,s\ \mathrm{occ}}
\int_{S(\mathcal{C})}\Omega_s^{(\tau)}\,d^2q.
\end{equation}
In the gapless limit $\Delta_\tau\to 0$ with a single valley enclosed, $\gamma_B=\pi$ (A148). Under weak staggered mass, the phase continuously deforms as
\begin{equation}
\gamma_B
=\pi\,\mathrm{sgn}(\Delta_\tau)\cdot\frac{|\Delta_\tau|}{\sqrt{v_D^2 q_{\rm loop}^2+\Delta_\tau^2}}
+\cdots
\end{equation}
for a circular loop of dual-route radius $q_{\rm loop}$. Leading linear response of $\gamma_B$ to $\Delta_{\rm stag}$ is dual-route pure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Stokes theorem converts the Berry connection integral into integrated curvature. Gapless limit recovers A148. Finite $\Delta_\tau$ softens the monopole; expansion in $\Delta_{\rm stag}$ at fixed $\Delta_0$ is elementary differentiation of~\eqref{eq:A151-Berry} (A148 formula with $\Delta_\tau$).
\end{proof}

\section{SN-A152 --- Dual-Matroid Classification}
\label{sec:SN-A152}
%==============================================================================

\subsection*{Scope}
(1) Complete dual-matroid classification under $H_{\rm cont}+D_{6h}$ (class C).
(2) State and prove the obstruction for unrestricted Grassmannian classification (class O documented).

\begin{definition}[Dual matroid pair]
\label{def:A152-dual}
A dual-matroid pair on a finite ground set $E$ is a pair $(\mathsf{M},\mathsf{M}^*)$ of matroids on the same $E$ such that the bases of $\mathsf{M}^*$ are the complements of the bases of $\mathsf{M}$ (standard matroid dual). In the packing-complement setting of A149,
\begin{equation}
\mathsf{M}_{15}^*
=\bigl(\mathsf{U}_{1,1}\oplus\mathsf{M}_{\rm eq}\oplus\mathsf{M}_{\rm cap}\bigr)^*
\simeq
\mathsf{U}_{0,1}\oplus\mathsf{M}_{\rm eq}^*\oplus\mathsf{M}_{\rm cap}^*,
\end{equation}
with ranks $\rho^*(\,A\,)=|A|-\rho_{\mathsf{M}}(E)+\rho_{\mathsf{M}}(E\setminus A)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Admissible dual-matroid class under $H_{\rm cont}$]
\label{def:A152-adm}
Let $\mathfrak{D}_{H}$ be the class of dual-matroid pairs $(\mathsf{M},\mathsf{M}^*)$ on ground sets of cardinality $N\le 40$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(D1)] perfect AF bipartite structure exists on an equatorial subset of even order $n$;
\item[(D2)] Maxwell soft-mode count soft$(n)=|n/2-3|$ vanishes (hence $n=6$);
\item[(D3)] duplex capacity: two polar shells of equal combinatorial rank;
\item[(D4)] orthogonal chord: shell cycle order $m$ satisfies $2\pi/m=\pi/2$ hence $m=4$;
\item[(D5)] crystallographic restriction: rotational orders in $\{1,2,3,4,6\}$;
\item[(D6)] free-energy Hessian nondegeneracy on the packing kernel (H3 of A149).
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Complete classification under $H_{\rm cont}+D_{6h}$]
\label{thm:A152-class}
Up to isomorphism of dual-matroid pairs,
\begin{equation}
\mathfrak{D}_{H}
=\bigl\{\,(\mathsf{M}_{15},\mathsf{M}_{15}^*)\,\bigr\}.
\end{equation}
That is, the unique dual-matroid pair admitted by $H_{\rm cont}+D_{6h}$ is the M15 packing-complement matroid of A149 and its dual. Rank triple $(r_{\rm pack},r_{\rm eq},r_{\rm cap})=(2,6,8)$ with $N^*=15$ is forced.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
From (D2): soft$(n)=0$ and even $n$ $\Rightarrow$ $n=6$ uniquely (A141). From (D4): $m=4$ uniquely. From (D3): $n_{\rm caps}=2$. Hence $N^*=1+6+2\cdot 4=15$ (A142). The equatorial exchange $B_{\rm eq}$ is the unique (up to simultaneous row/column sign flips and cyclic relabelling) nondegenerate AF quiver on $C_6$ compatible with Maxwell 3-pair covering: three dimers, soft modes zero. Cap matroid is the direct sum of two rank-$4$ graphic matroids of $C_4$ (orthogonal duplex). Centre is $\mathsf{U}_{1,1}$. Dual is uniquely determined by the basis-complement construction. Any other ground set cardinality fails (D2)--(D4). Any other exchange orientation either breaks AF bipartiteness (D1) or reintroduces soft modes (D2). Hessian nondegeneracy (D6) excludes null directions that would identify distinct pairs. Therefore $\mathfrak{D}_{H}$ is a singleton.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Obstruction: unrestricted Grassmannian dual-matroid]
\label{thm:A152-unrestricted}
Let $\mathrm{Gr}(k,N)$ be the real Grassmannian of $k$-planes in $\mathbb{R}^N$. The class of dual-matroid pairs induced by totally nonnegative cells of positroid stratifications of $\mathrm{Gr}(k,N)$ for unrestricted $(k,N)$ is infinite. No finite uniqueness theorem holds without (D1)--(D6) or equivalent selection axioms. In particular, unrestricted dual-matroid classification over the Grassmannian remains OPEN and is not closable by dual-route free-energy alone.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Positroid cells of $\mathrm{Gr}(k,N)$ are classified by decorated permutations; their number grows without bound as $N\to\infty$ (Postnikov). Each cell determines a matroid (and dual). Dual-route free-energy supplies continuous weights on a fixed packing skeleton but does not cut the discrete infinite family of positroids down to one without combinatorial selection axioms equivalent to (D1)--(D6). Explicit counterexamples at small $N$: the uniform matroid $\mathsf{U}_{k,N}$ and its dual for all $1\le k\le N-1$ are admissible as abstract dual pairs without AF/Maxwell constraints. Hence unrestricted classification is infinite and OPEN.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[What is closed vs open]
\label{cor:A152-split}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
\toprule
Statement & Status \\
\midrule
Dual-matroid uniqueness in $\mathfrak{D}_{H}$ & C \\
$\mathsf{M}_{15}$ isomorphism type under $H_{\rm cont}+D_{6h}$ & C \\
Unrestricted Grassmannian dual-matroid uniqueness & O (obstructed as unique) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\end{corollary}
